info.description: AstroDynamics Mission Planner — HTTP API served by `cargo run --bin mission-server`

get.summary: Body catalog — all supported target bodies with physics properties
Heliocentric state vector for a catalog body at an epoch
get.description: Only ANISE/DE440S-covered bodies (Mercury, Venus, Earth, Moon, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn) return a real state — small bodies in the catalog (Bennu, Apophis, Ryugu, Eros, Didymos,...) have no fixed ephemeris and return 422, since their position is only known via a mission's own [target_body.keplerian_orbit], which this generic endpoint has no access to. Known gap: querying "Sun" also 422s today even though DE440S covers it — anise_body in design.rs has no "sun" match arm yet.

Example mission config library — returns all preset MissionConfigs as JSON
get.description: Each preset is compiled from the example TOML files in MissionPlanner/config/ and returned with a derived id, display name, and one-line description. The config field is a full MissionConfig object that can be POSTed directly to /api/design/trajectory or /api/simulate.

post.summary: Validate a mission config — returns errors + structured summary
Run trajectory solver — Hohmann, Lambert porkchop, DiffCorrection, MonteCarlo, GA, or PSO
Run GNC sizing — selects hardware, sizes EKF, computes disturbance torques
Derived spacecraft mass properties (total mass, center of mass, full inertia tensor, per-component breakdown) and, optionally, per-plate SRP force vectors —
post.description: Pure computation, synchronous — no job/polling (cheap: closed-form bus-box + point-mass parallel-axis, no propagation). `com_m` and `inertia_kgm2` are computed about the spacecraft's TRUE center of mass; every position field elsewhere in MissionConfig (HardwareItem placement fields) is relative to the FIXED geometric-center origin (the bus centroid), NOT the CoM — see docs/MP/MANUAL.md §2.3 for the frame convention this enforces. inertia_kgm2 is a full symmetric 3x3 tensor (row-major) and is generally NOT diagonal once any component sits off-axis — do not assume only the 3 diagonal entries are meaningful. Set sun_hat_body to also get the srp field (per-plate force vectors from the real orbital_models flat-plate law, for live SRP-arrow rendering); omit it (or send null) to skip that section and get mass properties only.

Runs the same closed-loop machinery src/bin/sixdof_control_demo.rs verifies by hand (quaternion PD control law + mode-dependent control allocation, Phase 13d/13e) against a FIXED reference scenario (a circular Earth orbit at 700 km altitude, not user-configurable), driven by the real vehicle/actuator/gain values derived from the submitted config -- the same helpers run_streaming itself uses (build_spacecraft_properties, wheel_cluster_from_hardware, rcs_from_hardware, pd_gains_from_cfg). Synchronous, no job/polling: duration_s/tick_s are clamped server-side (tick 0.1-60 s, duration up to 7200 s) to keep wall-clock cost bounded. Use this for fast gain-tuning/actuator-sizing iteration before committing to a full /api/simulate run. See docs/MP/MANUAL.md section 7 for the governing control law/allocation math.

422.description: Invalid parameter (e.g. unknown control_mode, initial_error_deg out of [0,180])

post.summary: Start an async high-fidelity simulation job. Returns immediately with a job_id; the job runs in the background.
post.description: Branches on MissionConfig.cruise_seed FIRST, then simulation.monte_carlo_runs: cruise_seed set AND monte_carlo_runs > 0 (the design notes backlog item #10) starts a cruise Monte Carlo job -- disperses vehicle mass/inertia/reflectivity (cruise.rs::run_cruise_mc_streaming) across monte_carlo_runs cruise-loop runs; /stream carries CruiseMcRunMsg per *completed run* (never per-tick), /result returns CruiseMcSummaryResult, /steps returns {"runs": CruiseMcRunMsg[]}. cruise_seed set alone (monte_carlo_runs == 0, Phase 5.2) starts a single cruise-loop job — the Phase 13 translation+attitude+guidance composition (cruise.rs::run_cruise_leg) flown against a real Layer-1 reference trajectory, instead of the body-centric proximity-ops path; /stream carries CruiseStepMsg per control tick, /result returns CruiseResult, /steps returns {"steps": CruiseStepMsg[]}. Otherwise (cruise_seed not set): monte_carlo_runs == 0 (default) starts a single-run body-centric job — /stream carries SimStepMsg per measurement step, /result returns SimResult. monte_carlo_runs > 0 starts a body-centric Monte Carlo job instead — per the Monte Carlo streaming rule, this NEVER gets the per-step feed; /stream carries one McRunMsg per *completed run* (with a sparse trajectory only on a stride-selected subset, capped at 20 runs regardless of monte_carlo_runs), /result returns McSummaryResult, /steps returns {"runs": McRunMsg[]} instead of {"steps": SimStepMsg[]}. Same job_id/status/stream/steps/result endpoints serve all four kinds — the client already knows which kind it started. Phase 01/02 consistency: for either cruise job kind, this endpoint now integrates at the SAME simulation.rtol/atol Phase 01's own trajectory design used (previously hardcoded to 1e-10/1e-12 inside the cruise loop regardless of what was configured), and auto-populates cruise_seed.body_tracks with real ANISE-queried tracks for any target_body.third_bodies name not already present in the request (requires trajectory.departure_epoch to be set; silently adds nothing otherwise — best-effort, never an error) — so Phase 01's configured third-body perturbers carry over into the cruise simulation instead of silently disappearing.

get.summary: WebSocket upgrade — live feed, shape depends on job kind. Cruise MC jobs (cruise_seed set + monte_carlo_runs > 0): CruiseMcRunMsg per completed run. Cruise jobs (cruise_seed set alone): CruiseStepMsg per control tick. Single-run jobs: SimStepMsg per measurement step (dt_meas_s, not the denser dt_truth_s). Body-centric Monte Carlo jobs (monte_carlo_runs > 0): McRunMsg per completed run, never per truth-step. IMPORTANT, added after a real client crash: which of these four shapes a given job's stream carries is decided ENTIRELY by the request that started it (cruise_seed presence and monte_carlo_runs' value) — get that combination wrong (e.g. set cruise_seed and accidentally leave monte_carlo_runs at a stale nonzero default) and you'll get a completely different, unexpected shape back with no error. CruiseStepMsg/CruiseMcRunMsg both now carry a msg_type discriminant ("cruise_tick"/"cruise_mc_run") specifically so a client can check it before trusting the rest of a parsed frame, instead of assuming the shape matches the request it thought it made. Ends with a literal text frame "__DONE__" (not a clean WS close) — if the job already finished before the client connects, "__DONE__" is sent immediately rather than hanging (broadcast channels don't replay history to late subscribers, and fast sims often finish before the WS handshake completes).

101.description: Switching Protocols — each subsequent text frame is JSON-serialized CruiseMcRunMsg (cruise MC job), CruiseStepMsg (cruise job), SimStepMsg (single-run job), or McRunMsg (Monte Carlo job), until a final "__DONE__" text frame

get.summary: Full step/run history for a job, partial if still running. For replaying a run whose WS handshake didn't complete before the simulation finished (common for fast sims) — broadcast channels don't replay history to late subscribers, so the live stream alone can't recover this.
get.description: Shape depends on which kind of job job_id refers to: a cruise job (started with cruise_seed set, monte_carlo_runs == 0) or a single-run job both return {"steps": CruiseStepMsg[] | SimStepMsg[]}; a cruise MC job (cruise_seed set + monte_carlo_runs > 0) or a body-centric Monte Carlo job (monte_carlo_runs > 0 alone) both return {"runs": CruiseMcRunMsg[] | McRunMsg[]} instead.

get.summary: Final summary, only available once the job is done
get.description: Returns CruiseMcSummaryResult for a cruise MC job (cruise_seed set + monte_carlo_runs > 0), CruiseResult for a cruise job (cruise_seed set alone), SimResult for a single-run job, or McSummaryResult for a body-centric Monte Carlo job (monte_carlo_runs > 0 alone).

200.description: Cruise MC, cruise, simulation, or Monte Carlo result

post.summary: Request early stop for a running job (Phase 9k task 4). Idempotent — cancelling an already-finished job is a harmless no-op, not an error.
post.description: For a single-run job (monte_carlo_runs == 0), the truth-integration loop polls the cancellation flag every truth step (dt_truth_s), so this takes effect within roughly one truth step; /result then returns whatever telemetry was collected up to that point, not an error. For a Monte Carlo job (monte_carlo_runs > 0) this only affects /status reporting — the already-dispatched batch of runs is not interruptible with the current thread::scope-based implementation, a known and documented limitation, not an oversight.

post.summary: Start an async Phase 9 trajectory optimization job (real propagated dynamics — GA/PSO fitness includes actual numerical propagation under [optimization.force_model], NOT the closed-form Lambert proxy used by /api/design/trajectory's GA/PSO). Requires the config's `optimization` field to be set (non-null) — a config without it is rejected with 422.

422.description: Config validation errors, or missing [optimization] section

get.summary: Poll job progress. Unlike /api/simulate's status, total_steps is usually a known integer here (GA generations or PSO iterations come straight from the config), not always null.

WebSocket upgrade — live OptimizeStepMsg feed, one message per generation (GA) or iteration (PSO). Never carries a propagated arc per step (only the final /result does) — see the design notes Monte Carlo streaming rule, applied here too: an expensive value (a re-propagated arc) is computed once, not on every step. For MGA jobs, an MgaSequenceContextMsg frame (Phase 9k "step-stream context") is also interleaved — one per candidate flyby-body sequence, sent BEFORE that sequence's own OptimizeStepMsg frames. Ends with a literal text frame "__DONE__", same late-subscriber handling as /api/simulate/{job_id}/stream.

101.description: Switching Protocols — each subsequent text frame is JSON-serialized OptimizeStepMsg or (MGA only) MgaSequenceContextMsg — distinguish by the presence of msg_type (MgaSequenceContextMsg always has it, OptimizeStepMsg never does) — until a final "__DONE__" text frame

get.summary: Final result, only available once the job is done

500.description: Job failed — e.g. method = "MultipleShooting" (not implemented yet), or no valid solution at the best point

post.summary: Request early stop for a running job (Phase 9k task 4). Idempotent — cancelling an already-finished job is a harmless no-op, not an error.
post.description: Honored by GA/PSO (checked every generation/iteration and every refinement pass) — the job stops within roughly one generation and /result returns whatever candidate was best so far. NOT honored by MGA (method = "MGA") — cancelled is still recorded and reported by /status, but the DE search has no cancellation hook yet and runs to completion regardless.

post.summary: Run the Tisserand beam search only, and return every ranked candidate flyby sequence. Plain synchronous request/response — no job_id, no polling.
post.description: Wraps crate::sequence_search::run_sequence_search directly, without running the (much more expensive) ballistic grid scan or DE/MBH search that normally follow it in the MGA pipeline. Requires [optimization.mga.sequence_search] (candidate_bodies/max_legs/beam_width) to be present — [optimization.mga.flyby_bodies] is not used here, since the whole point of this endpoint is discovering flyby_bodies automatically. Fast enough (no propagation or Lambert solve per candidate) that a plain synchronous response is correct, unlike /api/mga-scan and /api/optimize which need the async-job pattern. Lets a caller see the full ranked field — not just the single top pick — before committing to the expensive full scan or DE search on one of them.

422.description: Config validation errors, or missing [optimization]/[optimization.mga]/[optimization.mga.sequence_search] section

post.summary: Start an async Phase 9w ballistic MGA window-scan job (deterministic, propagation-free — powered-flyby Lambert legs, no DSMs). Returns immediately with a job_id.
post.description: Wraps the mga-scan CLI (crate::mga_scan_run::mga_scan_api) — same async-job pattern as /api/optimize/simulate. Requires [optimization] with a fixed [optimization.mga] leg sequence (flyby_bodies, not sequence_search — run search-sequence/the Tisserand beam search first to pick a sequence for an auto-discovery mission) and an [optimization.mga.scan] section. A scan can take from seconds to several minutes depending on grid density (a real 4-leg VEEGA scan at 1,949 departure dates x 18 TOF points/leg took ~6 minutes). No WebSocket stream is offered — run_mga_scan has no per-evaluation progress hook, unlike GA/PSO/MGA-DE's generation loop, so there's nothing meaningful to stream; /status only reports running/done/error.

422.description: Config validation errors, or missing [optimization.mga.scan] section

get.summary: Poll job progress. No step counter (see /api/mga-scan's description) — running/error only.

Final result, only available once the job is done. Same fields mga_window_scan.csv already has, as a JSON array — also still written to disk as a side effect (mission's simulation.output_dir), same as every other async-job endpoint.

anise_covered.description: True if this body has real ephemeris coverage via GET /api/bodies/{name}/state. Always true for major bodies (Sun, Mercury, Venus, Earth, Moon, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn) via the always-present de440s.bsp. True for Phobos, Deimos, Europa, and Titan only if this server also has the relevant satellite kernel loaded (mar099s.bsp / jup365.bsp / sat441.bsp) -- check this field rather than assuming, since it's deployment-dependent. Always false for other small bodies (Bennu, Apophis, Ryugu, Eros, Didymos,...), which have no DE440S-family kernel at all.

pole_ra_deg.description: North pole right ascension [deg], ICRF/J2000 constant term. Null if no citable pole orientation is available (e.g. small bodies) — central-body gravity fidelity falls back to point-mass for those.

pole_dec_deg.description: North pole declination [deg], ICRF/J2000 constant term.

primary.description: The body this one actually orbits. Null means it orbits the Sun directly (true for every planet/asteroid). e.g. "Earth" for the Moon, "Jupiter" for Europa.

sma_m.description: Mean orbital semi-major axis around `primary` (or the Sun when primary is null) [m]. Null for the Sun and for small bodies whose full elements live in orbital_elements instead. Source: JPL Williams 2021 (planets) / JPL SSD satellite parameters (moons).

orbital_elements.description: Full HELIOCENTRIC Keplerian elements at a stated epoch (— real catalog-served orbit shapes so clients can draw true elliptical rings, including for small bodies with no ephemeris coverage, instead of hardcoding a client-side element table). Present for the 8 planets (Standish 1992 J2000 mean elements) and the 5 catalogued small bodies (JPL SBDB osculating elements at each body's stated epoch). Null for the Sun (frame origin) and for every moon — a moon's elements are primary-relative, a deliberately different contract not overloaded onto this heliocentric field.

OrbitalElements.description: Heliocentric Keplerian orbital elements at epoch_jd, referred to the MEAN ECLIPTIC AND EQUINOX OF J2000 (the native frame of both source tables) — NOT the equatorial ICRF frame /api/bodies/{name}/state vectors use; mixing the two requires rotating by the J2000 obliquity (23.43929111 deg). Mean/osculating elements at one epoch with no secular rates: intended for orbit rings and rough position estimates, not a substitute for real ephemeris where it exists.

epoch_jd.description: Epoch of the elements [Julian Date, TDB]. 2451545.0 (J2000.0) for planets; the JPL SBDB solution epoch for small bodies.

id.description: Kebab-case identifier matching the source TOML filename (without.toml)

name.description: Display name from [mission].name in the preset TOML

config.description: Full MissionConfig parsed from the preset TOML. Can be POSTed directly to /api/design/trajectory or /api/simulate.

power_w.description: Nominal operating power draw [W] — representative class estimate, not a specific flight unit's datasheet value.
Nominal valve-driver power draw [W] — representative class estimate.
Nominal operating power draw [W] — representative class estimate.

OpNavCameraSpec.description: Catalog grade — units are [rad], NOT [mrad]. Contrast with HardwareItem's OpNavCamera variant (bearing_noise_mrad/angular_size_noise_mrad), which is in mrad. This unit mismatch is real, not a typo — see hardware_catalog/src/sensor.rs vs MissionPlanner/src/config.rs.

power_w.description: Nominal operating power draw [W] — representative class estimate.

ImuSpec.description: IMU/accelerometer grade — ΔV measurement noise during impulsive manoeuvres. Medium grade matches the Bennu mission's IMU_DV_SIGMA_MPS constant.

power_w.description: Nominal operating power draw [W] — representative class estimate.

LidarSpec.description: LIDAR altimeter grade — slant-range measurement to the target body's surface. Medium grade matches the Bennu mission's LIDAR_SIGMA_M/LIDAR_MAX_RANGE_M constants.

max_range_m.description: Maximum operational range [m] — no return beyond this.

power_w.description: Nominal operating power draw [W] — representative class estimate.

LandmarkSensorSpec.description: Landmark-tracking (stereophotoclinometry-analogue) sensor grade — bearing-only line-of-sight measurements to catalogued surface features, giving full 3-D position from several simultaneous sightings without LIDAR. Distinct catalog item from OpNavCameraSpec despite similar optics, since it's sized against a different requirement (multi-landmark 3-D position knowledge).

catalog_size.description: Number of catalogued landmarks the processing pipeline can track.

power_w.description: Nominal operating power draw [W] — representative class estimate.

DsnLinkSpec.description: Deep Space Network ground-link grade — heliocentric uplink accuracy from ground orbit determination. Mass/power describe the onboard transponder + HGA terminal, not a ground asset.

power_w.description: Nominal operating power draw [W] — representative class estimate.

LaunchVehiclePerformancePoint.description: One verified (C3, injected mass) data point from a real flown mission — see hardware_catalog/src/launch_vehicle.rs for citations. NOT a smoothed vendor curve.

LaunchVehicleSpec.description: A launch vehicle's real C3-vs-injected-mass performance, built from one or more verified flown-mission data points, sorted by C3 ascending. Empty performance_points (Starship) means no real interplanetary payload has flown yet — not missing data to be estimated.

LaunchVehicleCheckApiResult.description: Feasibility of the configured launch vehicle ([spacecraft].launch_vehicle) delivering a trajectory's required departure C3 at the spacecraft's wet mass — the structured, API-facing form of what used to be CLI-only println! output. Added see the design notes. Only ever present (non-null at the parent field) for an Earth departure with a real, catalog-recognized vehicle configured — every other case (non-Earth departure, no vehicle configured, unrecognized name) is null at the parent field rather than a variant of this object, since there's no real vehicle to report a feasibility number for.

vehicle.description: Catalog name of the configured vehicle.

max_injected_mass_kg.description: Max mass [kg] the vehicle can inject at required_c3_km2s2, from its real flown-mission curve. Null if required_c3_km2s2 exceeds every verified data point for this vehicle (no extrapolation).

margin_kg.description: max_injected_mass_kg - spacecraft_mass_kg. Null whenever max_injected_mass_kg is null.

feasible.description: True only when the vehicle has verified performance data at this C3 AND can lift this wet mass.

max_c3_at_mass_km2s2.description: Partial coverage (Phase 14e): the maximum C3 [km²/s²] the vehicle gives THIS wet mass, from the inverse of its verified curve (clamped to the verified range — a light payload above the highest verified point reports that point's C3). Null when no verified point shows the vehicle lifting this mass to any escape energy.

parking_orbit_radius_m.description: Parking-orbit radius [m] the ΔV split below is referred to ([trajectory.departure].parking_orbit_radius_m, or the atmospheric/airless default).

launcher_departure_dv_ms.description: Departure ΔV [m/s] the launcher delivers from that parking orbit: √(C3_L + 2μ/r_p) − √(μ/r_p) with C3_L = min(max_c3_at_mass_km2s2, required_c3_km2s2). The full tangential escape burn when the launcher covers the C3; 0 when it cannot lift the mass at all.

onboard_departure_dv_ms.description: Perigee top-up [m/s] the spacecraft adds from the same periapsis: √(C3_req + 2μ/r_p) − √(C3_L + 2μ/r_p). 0 when the launcher covers the C3; the whole escape burn when it cannot lift the mass.

reason.description: Why feasible is false, when it is: distinguishes 'required C3 exceeds the vehicle's verified performance range' from 'the vehicle cannot lift this wet mass at the required C3' (and 'no verified interplanetary performance data' for a vehicle with an empty curve). Null when feasible.

LaunchGeometryApiResult.description: Closed-form launch geometry from a departure asymptote (Phase 14c, trajectory_solver::launch_geometry; MANUAL.md §13.6). For fixed v∞ and periapsis the escape hyperbola is a one-parameter family (rotation about the asymptote), so the plane is chosen after the interplanetary solve to satisfy the site: i ≥ |DLA| (contains the asymptote) and i ≥ |site latitude| (no dogleg). No ascent is modelled — the parking-orbit coast and injection state are physical, the ascent a frontend schematic. Angles in degrees; vectors body-relative inertial (ICRF/J2000).

site_lat_deg.description: Site geodetic latitude [deg], positive north — the only site quantity in the physics.

site_lon_deg.description: Site longitude [deg], positive east — display / future daily-window use.

rla_deg.description: Right ascension of the launch asymptote [deg], body equatorial frame, [0, 360).

inclination_deg.description: Inclination of the parking/escape plane to the body equator [deg] — the configured [trajectory.departure].inclination_deg, or the minimum feasible one.

min_inclination_deg.description: max(|DLA|, |site latitude|) [deg] — the cheapest plane that contains the asymptote and needs no dogleg.

feasible_no_dogleg.description: inclination_deg ≥ min_inclination_deg. False = the requested plane needs a dogleg from this site; reported infeasible, never priced.

launch_azimuth_deg.description: Launch azimuth from north [deg] for the ascending (north-east-going) pass: sin β = cos i / cos φ. The descending alternative is 180 − β.

raan_deg.description: Right ascension of the parking orbit's ascending node [deg], body equatorial frame.

coast_angle_deg.description: In-plane angle coasted in the parking orbit from the site's ascending crossing to the injection periapsis [deg]. Schematic: the ascent's own downrange angle is not modelled.

parking_orbit_radius_m.description: Parking / injection radius [m] (185 km default altitude in Launch mode).

injection_r_m.description: Injection point (periapsis of the escape hyperbola), body-relative inertial [m].

injection_v_mps.description: Velocity after the injection burn, body-relative inertial [m/s]; |v|² − 2μ/r_p = v∞² exactly.

parking_v_mps.description: Parking-orbit circular velocity at the injection point before the burn [m/s].

DvLedgerApiResult.description: Two-pool ΔV ledger + propellant feasibility for one trajectory (Phase 14e MANUAL.md §13.5). Every ΔV is paid from the LAUNCHER pool (the upper stage's injection, priced against the vehicle's verified C3-vs-mass curve — Earth departure with a catalog vehicle only) or the ONBOARD pool (Isp·g₀·ln(m_wet/m_dry): the departure remainder, every DSM, and ALWAYS the arrival burn). Partial launcher coverage is real: a vehicle short of the required C3 still delivers its maximum at this mass and the spacecraft tops up from the same periapsis (see LaunchVehicleCheckApiResult). Computed by ONE shared helper for every result type, so BestArcApiResult/OptimizerApiResult/OptimizeApiResult ledgers are directly comparable.

departure_dv_ms.description: Full departure burn [m/s] from the parking orbit before any split (the tangential escape burn for the narrowing stage and MGA; the search's own, generally non-tangential, dv_departure_ms for single-leg GA/PSO).

departure_dv_pool.description: Who pays the departure burn: fully the launcher, fully onboard (no launcher share at all), or split (launcher at its maximum C3 for this mass, spacecraft tops up).

launcher_dv_ms.description: Departure ΔV [m/s] delivered by the launch vehicle — 0 without one.

onboard_departure_dv_ms.description: Departure ΔV [m/s] the spacecraft's own engine must add.

onboard_arrival_dv_ms.description: Arrival/capture burn [m/s] — always onboard; 0 for a Flyby.

onboard_dsm_dv_ms.description: Deep-space maneuvers [m/s] (sum of mga_dv_dsms_ms for MGA) — always onboard; 0 for a single-leg transfer.

onboard_dv_available_ms.description: Isp·g₀·ln(m_wet/m_dry) [m/s]. Null when no [spacecraft.propulsion] is configured (the three fields below are then null too).

onboard_propellant_required_kg.description: Propellant the onboard requirement consumes, m_wet·(1 − e^(−Δv/(Isp·g₀))) [kg] — compare with [spacecraft].propellant_mass_kg.

mass_ratio_required.description: m_wet/m_dry the onboard requirement demands, e^(Δv/(Isp·g₀)) — a scale-free feasibility figure (chemical stages top out around 10–15).

budget_margin_ms.description: onboard_dv_available_ms − onboard_dv_required_ms [m/s]; positive = onboard margin remaining. The same number the parent's legacy budget_margin_ms carries.

launch_vehicles.description: Added. Only meaningful for an Earth departure ([trajectory].departure_body) — see LaunchVehicleCheckApiResult.

name.description: Body name — looked up in catalog; fields below override catalog values

ephemeris.description: The accepted tag is "Anise" (PascalCase serde default) — NOT "ANISE". Other casings, including the all-caps form, return 400.

pole_ra_deg.description: North pole right ascension [deg], ICRF/J2000. Overrides the catalog value if set; resolved from the catalog by body name otherwise. Needed for real J2/J2J3J4 central-body fidelity when this body becomes the propagator's central body — see /api/bodies' field of the same name.

pole_dec_deg.description: North pole declination [deg], ICRF/J2000. See pole_ra_deg.

HardwareItem.description: Internally tagged (serde tag = "type") union — one entry per [[spacecraft.hardware]] TOML block. Was undocumented before (generated frontend type was `{type} & Record<string, unknown>`, hiding even CustomPlate's real fields) — same class of drift as the MgaParams fix. Placement extension (spacecraft-builder design): CustomPlate, RcsThruster, and CommAntenna (new) all have real body-frame placement; StarTracker/OpNavCamera/Lidar/SolarPanel gained optional placement/boresight fields (None = unplaced, Phase-1-honest generic rendering). ReactionWheelCluster/IMU intentionally have none — see each schema's own description for why.

mass_kg.description: PER-WHEEL mass [kg] (derived-mass-properties extension). null falls back to the matching hardware_catalog::ReactionWheelSpec grade's mass_kg. No placement field on this variant — wheels are assumed to sit at the spacecraft's geometric-center origin for the mass-properties rollup.

HardwareItemReactionWheelCluster.description: No placement field, deliberately — cluster GEOMETRY (orthogonal vs. pyramid + cant angle), not position, is what matters for a momentum-exchange device; per-wheel position/orientation is not modeled. The backend's ReactionWheelCluster is fixed at [f64;4] (4-wheel pyramid) — a real N-wheel generalization is deferred (Phase 13f note).

moment_arm_m.description: Scalar moment arm [m] — the AGGREGATE cluster model (a canonical symmetric 12-thruster layout). Used by simulate.rs::rcs_from_hardware ONLY as a fallback when no RcsThruster entries (see that schema) are present in the same config — real placed thrusters take precedence,.

mass_kg.description: PER-THRUSTER mass [kg]. null falls back to hardware_catalog::ThrusterSpec::monoprop.mass_kg. No placement field (aggregate cluster) — same geometric-center-origin assumption as ReactionWheelCluster.mass_kg.

position_m.description: Thruster position relative to spacecraft CoM, body frame [m].

direction.description: Thrust direction — the direction of the FORCE applied to the spacecraft (same convention as BurnConfig::body_dir, not the nozzle/exhaust direction), body frame. Normalized on load.

mass_kg.description: This thruster's own mass [kg]. null falls back to hardware_catalog::ThrusterSpec::monoprop.mass_kg.

isp_s.description: This thruster's own specific impulse [s] — added. null falls back to hardware_catalog::ThrusterSpec::monoprop.isp_s, same convention as mass_kg. sim_engine::control::allocate prices RCS propellant per-thruster from this value (each thruster's own thrust_n/isp_s and the duty cycle it individually fired at), not against one aggregate scalar for the whole set — so a real layout mixing thruster classes (e.g. fine ColdGas thrusters for pointing alongside a higher-thrust Monoprop set for coarse slews) accounts for propellant honestly.

HardwareItemRcsThruster.description: One real, individually-placed RCS thruster. Consumed by the LIVE 6DOF simulation as of: simulate.rs::rcs_from_hardware builds the sim's actual actuator list directly from these entries, exactly as placed, whenever any are present — a genuinely asymmetric or incomplete-coverage layout is realized as-is (not smoothed into a symmetric-cluster equivalent), which is what makes an attitude-stability preview built on top of it honest. Falls back to the aggregate RCS variant only when no RcsThruster entries exist in the config.

boresight.description: Boresight direction, body frame (unit; normalized on load). null = unplaced (Phase 1: rendered generically, no pointing geometry).

position_m.description: Sensor position relative to spacecraft CoM, body frame [m]. Cosmetic only (no parallax effect modeled at spacecraft scale).

fov_deg.description: Full field-of-view half-angle [deg], for the FOV-cone render and occlusion warnings. null = no cone rendered.

mass_kg.description: Unit mass [kg]. null falls back to the matching hardware_catalog::StarTrackerSpec grade's mass_kg.

noise_sigma_mps.description: 1-sigma delta-V noise per axis per step [m/s].

mass_kg.description: Unit mass [kg]. null falls back to hardware_catalog::ImuSpec::medium.mass_kg.

HardwareItemIMU.description: No placement field, deliberately — an IMU measures the spacecraft's own rigid-body motion, which has no dependence on where in the body it sits (to first order, ignoring lever-arm effects this model doesn't represent).

bearing_noise_mrad.description: 1-sigma bearing noise [mrad]. NOTE: a different unit from OpNavCameraSpec's bearing_noise_rad ([rad]) returned by GET /api/hardware — same physical quantity, inconsistent units between request and catalog response, known issue, not yet reconciled.

angular_size_noise_mrad.description: 1-sigma angular-size noise [mrad]. See bearing_noise_mrad's unit note.

boresight.description: Boresight direction, body frame (unit; normalized on load). null = unplaced.

position_m.description: Camera position relative to spacecraft CoM, body frame [m].

fov_deg.description: Full field-of-view half-angle [deg]. null = no cone rendered.

mass_kg.description: Unit mass [kg]. null falls back to the matching hardware_catalog::OpNavCameraSpec grade's mass_kg.

boresight.description: Boresight direction, body frame (unit; normalized on load). null = unplaced.

position_m.description: Sensor position relative to spacecraft CoM, body frame [m].

fov_deg.description: Full field-of-view half-angle [deg]. null = no cone rendered.

mass_kg.description: Unit mass [kg]. null falls back to the matching hardware_catalog::LidarSpec grade's mass_kg.

boresight.description: Boresight direction, body frame (unit; normalized on load).

beamwidth_deg.description: Full beamwidth [deg] (half-angle of the comm cone — same convention as fov_deg elsewhere, named differently here since "beamwidth" is the standard RF term).

position_m.description: Antenna position relative to spacecraft CoM, body frame [m]. Cosmetic only.

mass_kg.description: Unit mass [kg]. null falls back to a representative HGA-class default (no dedicated antenna catalog exists yet).

HardwareItemCommAntenna.description: Comm antenna (HGA/LGA) — added (no prior representation existed). Renders identically to a star-tracker/camera boresight cone. Sets up the classic simultaneous-pointing-constraint problem (panels at Sun + HGA at Earth + camera at target) for the Phase 03 pointing-mode/attitude-commander work.

area_m2.description: Total panel area [m^2] — used directly for the unplaced/aggregate case (existing behavior, unchanged); ignored in favor of width_m*height_m when a placed panel supplies both.

position_m.description: Panel geometric centre relative to spacecraft CoM, body frame [m]. Placement extension — set together with normal to make this a real placed, SRP-force-contributing panel (its own Plate) instead of an unplaced entry feeding the automatic symmetric +/-y panel pair.

normal.description: Deployed outward normal, body frame (unit; normalized on load). See position_m.

width_m.description: Panel width [m] (in-plane). With height_m, overrides area_m2 for the plate this panel contributes.

articulation.description: Articulation mechanism (refined, see docs/MP/MANUAL.md §6.5) — null = fixed (body-mounted, no articulation; panel normal is a hard spacecraft-attitude constraint). Schema-only for now, not yet consumed by any solver.

rho_s.description: Specular reflectivity, 0-1, for a PLACED panel's own Plate. Defaults to 0.08 when omitted. Ignored for an unplaced entry.

rho_d.description: Diffuse reflectivity, 0-1, for a PLACED panel. Defaults to 0.10. See rho_s.

mass_kg.description: TOTAL panel mass [kg] (both wings, if this entry represents a pair). null falls back to area * hardware_catalog::PanelSpec::rigid.areal_density_kgm2 (area = width_m*height_m if both given, else area_m2).

HardwareItemSolarPanel.description: The canonical placed-panel representation is "own fields" (this variant), not CustomPlate — decided because the builder mockup review wants independent live width_m/height_m resize handles and an articulation flag, neither of which CustomPlate represents. An unplaced entry (position_m/normal both null, every previous config) behaves exactly as before.

PanelArticulation.description: Internally tagged (serde tag = "kind") union nested inside HardwareItemSolarPanel.articulation — the three real solar-array-drive mechanism classes (docs/MP/MANUAL.md §6.5). A bare-fixed panel is represented by articulation being null on the parent, not a variant of this union.

axis.description: Single rotation axis, body frame (unit; normalized on load). Exact Sun-tracking only when the Sun lies in the plane perpendicular to this axis — otherwise a real cosine loss.

axis1.description: First rotation axis, body frame (unit; normalized on load). Must not be (nearly) parallel to axis2.

axis2.description: Second rotation axis, body frame (unit; normalized on load). A real Solar Array Drive Assembly — in the idealized unconstrained-range case, fully decouples panel pointing from spacecraft attitude.

normal.description: Outward unit normal in the body frame [x, y, z] (normalized on load — need not be pre-normalized).

center_offset_m.description: Plate geometric centre relative to spacecraft CoM, body frame [m]. Required for SRP torque: tau_i = center_i x F_i.

rho_s.description: Specular reflectivity, 0-1. Defaults to 0.30 (matching the automatic bus faces) when omitted.

rho_d.description: Diffuse reflectivity, 0-1. Defaults to 0.20 (matching the automatic bus faces) when omitted.

double_sided.description: Illuminated from either side (e.g. a deployable dish or panel-like plate) vs. only its outward face (e.g. a bus-mounted instrument cover). Defaults to false (single-sided) when omitted.

mass_kg.description: Plate mass [kg]. null falls back to a rough generic areal-density placeholder (CustomPlate represents an arbitrary shape with no natural structural class).

HardwareItemCustomPlate.description: The only HardwareItem variant with real body-frame placement today (Phase 13a). Adds one arbitrary flat plate to the spacecraft's FlatPlate/NPlate SRP geometry, on top of the automatic 6 bus faces and any SolarPanel entries — lets a mission describe shapes more complex than a box + symmetric panel pair (dish antenna, asymmetric deployable, instrument cover). Maps directly onto orbital_models::acceleration::srp::Plate.

derive_inertia_from_geometry.description: When true, the live 6DOF simulation uses the diagonal of the real parallel-axis-derived inertia tensor (bus box + every placed/itemized HardwareItem, about the true center of mass -- same computation POST /api/design/vehicle already exposes) instead of this struct's own inertia_diag_kgm2. Default/null/false: inertia_diag_kgm2 stays authoritative, byte-for-byte the previous behavior. Off-diagonal (cross-coupling) terms are not used -- the live sim's SpacecraftProperties is diagonal-only.

target_orbit_radius_m.description: Capture orbit radius at the arrival body [m]. When capture_eccentricity > 0 this is the capture orbit's PERIAPSIS radius.

capture_eccentricity.description: Capture orbit eccentricity in [0, 1) (Phase 9v-ii). Default 0.0 = circular capture. When > 0 the LOI burn is applied at periapsis into an ellipse: dv = sqrt(v_inf^2 + 2*mu/r_p) - sqrt(mu*(1+e)/r_p). The GTOP Cassini-2 benchmark uses r_p = 108950 km, e = 0.98.

CruiseConfig.description: Search-space window for the narrowing-stage solvers (GridSearch/MonteCarlo/GA/PSO) under /api/design/trajectory. All fields optional with defaults applied server-side — this schema was previously missing from the spec even though MissionPlanner/src/config.rs::TrajectoryConfig has carried it since before Phase 9.

tof_days_min.description: Minimum time-of-flight to search [days]. Defaults to 100.0 if omitted.

tof_days_max.description: Maximum time-of-flight to search [days]. Defaults to 400.0 if omitted.

grid_resolution.description: Number of grid points per axis for the porkchop scan. Defaults to 30 if omitted.

departure_window_days.description: Width of the departure window to sweep [days], centered on trajectory.departure_epoch. Defaults to 60.0 if omitted.

start_s.description: Window start [s on the reference clock], >= 0.

initial_dr_m.description: Optional position dispersion [m] added to the reference state at start_s.

initial_dv_mps.description: Optional velocity dispersion [m/s] added to the reference state at start_s.

DepartureConfig.description: [trajectory.departure] (Phase 8e parking radius; Phase 14a departure mode). Every field optional — an empty object is ParkingOrbit with the default parking radius (body_radius + 200 km if atmospheric, 1.5 × radius if airless).

parking_orbit_radius_m.description: Parking-orbit radius [m] the escape burn is sized from. Overrides both the atmospheric/airless default and, in Launch mode, parking_altitude_m.

mode.description: ParkingOrbit: the spacecraft starts in the given orbit and the departure burn is onboard (single-leg search genes theta/dv/phi unchanged). Launch: the mission starts from launch_site; the launcher's upper stage delivers the injection (departure ΔV = launcher pool, capture + DSMs onboard), the search's departure genes become (v∞, RLA, DLA) and the parking orbit / injection are closed-form launch geometry (MANUAL.md §13.6). Launch requires spacecraft.launch_vehicle, launch_site, and a departure body with a catalog pole (422 otherwise).

launch_site.description: Required in Launch mode. Only the latitude enters the physics.

parking_altitude_m.description: Launch mode: altitude of the parking orbit reached by the ascent before the upper-stage burn [m]. Default 185,000 (~100 n.mi.). Must be > 0.

inclination_deg.description: Launch mode: explicit parking/escape-plane inclination to the departure body's equator [deg, 0–180]. Omit for the minimum feasible plane max(|DLA|, |site latitude|). Below the site latitude = dogleg → launch_geometry.feasible_no_dogleg = false (never priced).

lon_deg.description: Longitude [deg], positive east. Display / future daily-launch-window use only.

solver.description: GridSearch is Lambert's porkchop scan exposed under a separate name (identical dispatch). SA/ManifoldStitch/WSB are recognized but return an error from /api/design/trajectory today — implemented in other, unconnected codebases (OptimizationProblems / AstroProbs/LunarTrajectories).

departure_body.description: Catalog body name. Now required (previously optional with a silent "Earth" fallback) — departure economics (launch-vehicle-provided vs. self-funded escape burn) and the real parking-orbit departure leg both depend on which body this is.

departure.description: [trajectory.departure] — parking-orbit radius and, since Phase 14a, the departure MODE (ParkingOrbit | Launch) with its launch site. Omit for the historical ParkingOrbit behaviour with the default parking radius.

cruise.description: Search-space window for GridSearch/MonteCarlo/GA/PSO. This is the field the frontend needs to expose to actually narrow the search — see CruiseConfig.

reaction_wheel_kp.description: Legacy explicit wheel-PD proportional gain override [N·m/rad]; honored when attitude_control.wheels is absent. Omit for the derived value (MANUAL.md §10.1).

reaction_wheel_kd.description: Legacy explicit wheel-PD derivative gain override [N·m·s/rad].

attitude_control.description: Three-layer attitude control (MANUAL.md §10.5): per-actuator law, per-activity tuning, gain scheduling. Optional; omitted = fully derived from the vehicle. The values actually used come back in CruiseResult.attitude_control_effective.

AttitudeControlConfig.description: gnc.attitude_control — every field optional. Layer 1: wheels (default Pd derived from the wheel cluster's max_torque) and thrusters (default Pid derived from the placed RCS layout's worst-axis torque authority — integral action removes the steady-state offset a persistent engine-misalignment torque leaves under pure PD; PhasePlane is the thruster-native alternative). Layer 2: activities. Layer 3: gain_scheduling.

activities.description: Per-activity tuning overrides (MANUAL.md §10.5.4). Defaults: hold 1.0/1.0, slew 1.0/1.0, burn_hold 1.0/0.5, coast 0.5/2.0 (bandwidth_scale/deadband_scale).

gain_scheduling.description: Layer 3 (MANUAL.md §10.5.5). enabled (default true): re-derive the active law on mode/activity change or when mass moves by more than mass_change_fraction (default 0.05) of the reference mass. inertia_scales_with_mass (default false): model the scheduling inertia as I_ref·m/m_ref — off by default because the truth propagator holds inertia constant through propellant depletion; enabling it is a deliberate controller/truth mismatch until the truth model carries a propellant-inertia term.

AttitudeLawConfig.description: One layer-1 law, tagged on `law`. Every parameter optional = derived default for that actuator class. Angles in degrees.

integral_limit.description: Pid: anti-windup clamp on |∫θ dt| per axis [rad·s] (default τ_authority/k_i).

deadband_deg.description: PhasePlane: switching-function deadband δ (default 0.5°). Must exceed τ_auth·t_min·T/I or the minimum impulse bit sets a larger limit cycle (warned).

min_on_time_s.description: PhasePlane: minimum thruster on-time / impulse bit [s] (default 0.02).

lead_time_s.description: PhasePlane: lead time T in s = θ + T·ω [s] (default 2·k_d/k_p of the derived PD).

bandwidth_scale.description: Multiplies closed-loop ω_n (k_p→s²k_p, k_d→s·k_d, k_i→s³k_i, T→T/s); damping ratio invariant.

AttitudeLawReport.description: Effective parameters of one layer-1 law as flown (CruiseResult.attitude_control_effective). source is 'derived' or 'config'. Nulls: PD/PID have no deadband fields, PhasePlane has no gains/ω_n/ζ.

authority_nm.description: Worst-axis torque authority the law was derived against [N·m].

omega_n_radps.description: Closed-loop natural frequency at the reference max inertia.

settling_time_s.description: ≈ 4/(ζ·ω_n); what the burn executive adds to its slew lead time.

warnings.description: e.g. a phase-plane deadband smaller than its minimum-impulse-bit limit cycle, or zero RCS authority on some axis.

GainSchedulePoint.description: Layer-3 schedule point — recorded on each tick the active law was (re)derived (mode/activity change or mass trigger).

optimization.description: Phase 9 trajectory optimization stage (Layer 1b — real propagated dynamics). Null/omitted means this mission doesn't use the optimization stage; /api/optimize then rejects with 422.

cruise_seed.description: Phase 5.2 (roadmap item 13i). When set, POST /api/simulate flies the Phase 13 translation+attitude+guidance cruise composition seeded from a real Layer-1 design/optimize result, instead of the body-centric proximity-ops path. Null/omitted (the default) preserves the existing body-centric behavior completely unchanged.

r_m.description: Heliocentric position [m] — same frame as design.rs's ArcApiPoint.

v_mps.description: Heliocentric velocity [m/s]. Not carried by ArcApiPoint today — the client is expected to have retained it from whatever real propagation produced the reference (e.g. a design/optimize result's own internal arc, before its velocity was dropped for the ArcApiPoint wire format).

reference.description: The Layer-1 trajectory to track — dispersion (dr_m) is always reported against this; when tcm_dr_threshold_m is set, it is also actively corrected via threshold-triggered TCM burns (item 5) targeting this same reference's own endpoint. At least 2 points, sorted ascending by t_s, with reference[0].t_s == 0 and reference[0].r_m/v_mps matching r0_m/v0_m within 1 m / 1 mm/s (check_config rejects otherwise — a mismatched start would silently report a nonzero dispersion at t=0 unrelated to real tracking quality).

duration_s.description: How long to fly the leg [s]. Must not exceed the reference's own time span.

tick_s.description: Control-loop tick [s]. Must respect the vehicle/gains' closed-loop bandwidth (roughly tick <= natural_period/10..20, natural_period ~ 2*pi*sqrt(inertia/kp)) — check_config cannot verify this without duplicating that computation, so an unstable choice surfaces at runtime (divergent pointing error, integrator warnings), not as a validation error. See cruise_demo.rs's doc comment for the real incident (a 3600 s tick genuinely destabilized a real vehicle/gains combination) that established this constraint.

modes.description: Phase 03 — named, prioritized pointing-rule sets. Empty (the default) preserves the pre-ask-#7 behavior exactly: a fixed SunPointing attitude hold for the whole leg. See docs/MP/MANUAL.md §6.4 for why only the top 2 rules in any one mode can ever control the attitude — rule 3+ are evaluated and reported as satisfied/violated, never controlling.

mode_schedule.description: Time-windowed assignment of modes (by name) to the leg's timeline. A tick not covered by any entry falls back to safe_mode if set, else to the legacy fixed SunPointing behavior. Overlapping entries: the LAST matching entry (list order) wins.

safe_mode.description: Name of a mode (must exist in modes) used for any tick not covered by mode_schedule — entered by schedule-gap fallback in this first cut, not real fault detection (no fault-detection system exists in this codebase yet).

body_tracks.description: Precomputed heliocentric position tracks for any PointingTargetConfig Body target referenced by a rule in modes (Earth, the target body, a flyby body,...) — supplied by the client, same reasoning as reference itself (cruise.rs is deliberately ANISE-free). Since a track with a resolvable mu_m3s2 ALSO becomes a real third-body gravitational perturber, not just a pointing target — see BodyTrackConfig.mu_m3s2. POST /api/simulate also auto-appends a real track for any target_body.third_bodies name not already present here (server-side, via design::build_third_body_tracks) — this array as SENT in the request need not include those names, but the request's cruise_seed as ACTUALLY RUN will.

tcm_dr_threshold_m.description: Item 5 hardened (Phase 13m-13p): trigger a trajectory-correction maneuver the first tick position dispersion (dr_m) exceeds this [m], subject to a cooldown after the previous correction and a minimum-remaining-TOF floor. null (default) preserves the exact pre-TCM coast-only behavior. Requires spacecraft.propulsion to also be set (the thrust/Isp source for the burn) — check_config flags this combination as an error if propulsion is missing, since it would otherwise silently never fire. The correction targets a NEARER epoch than the fixed leg-end whenever that's more than a quarter of the vehicle's current local orbital period away (Phase 13p — a single-revolution Lambert solve forced to satisfy a multi-revolution time-of-flight is genuinely ill-posed, not just imprecise), re-solved continuously while reorienting (the reorientation itself can take real time, independent of main-engine thrust, during which a one-shot solve would go stale). Takes priority over pointing_mode/modes for the whole maneuver (Slewing to burn attitude, then Burning, or — for a small correction, or a pointing_locked mode — an RCS-only correction that does NOT override pointing), and is NOT guaranteed to complete within duration_s if the demanded DeltaV exceeds what spacecraft.propulsion can deliver in the remaining time — see CruiseStepMsg.tcm_phase.

burn_tick_s.description: Mode-scheduled control tick [s] used while a main-engine burn is FIRING (MANUAL.md §10.5.1): the discrete-loop margin caps attitude bandwidth at ω_n ≤ 2π/(15·tick), so a coarse cruise tick makes the thrusters' larger torque authority unusable during burns regardless of the law. The thruster-mode law is derived at THIS tick. Default when omitted: max(tick_s/10, 1 s), never longer than tick_s. Must satisfy 0 < burn_tick_s <= tick_s.

window.description: Test window: fly only [start_s, end_s] of the leg. The truth starts at the REFERENCE state at start_s (plus the optional dispersion), r0_m/v0_m are ignored, planned burns before start_s are skipped, the tank is assumed full at start_s. For testing an approach-phase or burn change without flying the whole cruise. Null = the whole leg (unchanged behaviour).

report_stride_maneuver.description: Phase-adaptive reporting: stride used INSTEAD of report_stride on fast-dynamics ticks — any Slewing/Burning/RcsCorrecting tick, any tick inside a registered SOI-capture body's sphere (parking coast, capture orbit — the frontend's jagged-parking-polygon and attitude-swing-between-samples symptoms), plus every tick within a 600 s trailing window after a tcm_phase or active_mode transition (the transition tick itself always relays). Default 1 = full control-loop resolution there while cruise coast keeps the coarse budgeted stride; those windows are a small share of a mission so the total message count stays near the coast budget (the frontend's LTTB downsampling handles the rest). Relay-layer only: control-loop fidelity, max_dr_m, the on-disk CSV and mode_transitions are unaffected, exactly like report_stride.

report_stride.description: (frontend ask): decouples REPORTING cadence (the /api/simulate/:id/stream WS broadcast and the /steps REST history) from the real control-loop tick — only relay every Nth tick externally (plus always tick 0 and the final tick), while the control loop itself, max_dr_m/max_wheel_momentum_nms, the on-disk CSV, and mode_transitions all still run/compute at the full tick_s, completely unaffected. null or 1 both mean "report every tick" (the pre-existing behavior); check_config rejects 0. Needed because a long leg reported at full tick_s cadence can overflow a JSON string's max length client-side (confirmed: ERR_STRING_TOO_LONG on a real 129-day/tick_s=30 leg, ~371,500 ticks) — raising tick_s instead would also coarsen the control loop's own bandwidth, which this field deliberately does not touch. Trade-off: /cancel is only checked on reported ticks too, so worst-case cancel latency becomes report_stride * tick_s seconds instead of ~1 tick.

planned_burns.description: Phase 13n: scheduled burn EVENTS (a DSM on an MGA leg, an arrival/capture burn, a departure burn under GNC test) — as opposed to tcm_dr_threshold_m's REACTIVE, dispersion-triggered executive. Empty (default) preserves the exact pre-13n behavior. Fires via the SAME BurnAttitude + body-+X-fire mechanism the reactive executive uses, always through the main engine (never the RCS-only path) — takes priority over a reactive trigger on any tick both would fire. Requires spacecraft.propulsion, same as tcm_dr_threshold_m. Each entry's dv_inertial_mps fires verbatim by default; set that entry's target_epoch_s (see PlannedBurnConfig) to instead re-solve the fired ΔV fresh from the vehicle's real dispersed state at ignition — only meaningful for a DSM (a position target), not an arrival/capture or departure burn (which shape velocity, not position, and are not yet re-targetable).

PlannedBurnConfig.description: One scheduled burn event — see CruiseSeedConfig.planned_burns.

epoch_s.description: Mission-elapsed time to trigger this burn [s]. planned_burns must be sorted ascending by this field.

dv_inertial_mps.description: The ΔV to deliver, heliocentric/inertial frame [m/s] — direction and magnitude combined in one vector, straight from the adopted arc's own DSM/capture-burn fields. Fired verbatim unless target_epoch_s is set.

target_epoch_s.description: Nuance 2: when set, the ACTUAL fired ΔV is re-solved fresh at ignition from the vehicle's real current state, targeting the reference trajectory's own recorded position at this epoch [s since departure] via the same Lambert re-solve the reactive TCM executive uses — absorbing whatever dispersion has accumulated since the last correction, instead of firing dv_inertial_mps verbatim. Falls back to dv_inertial_mps if the fresh solve fails. Must be > epoch_s and <= cruise_seed.duration_s. Only meaningful for a DSM (a position target) — leave null for an arrival/capture or departure burn, which shape velocity, not position.

external_stage.description: : this burn is delivered by an EXTERNAL stage (a launch vehicle's upper stage for an Earth departure — the launcher-provided ΔV pool of the two-pool model, LaunchVehicleCheck), not the spacecraft's engine: applied impulsively (dv_inertial_mps verbatim) at epoch_s with no slew, no spacecraft-attitude requirement and NO draw on propellant_mass_kg. Set it on the departure burn whenever launch_vehicle_check.feasible is true for the adopted trajectory; otherwise a Phase-03 replay fires the multi-km/s injection through the onboard engine and drains the tank before cruise begins. Reported as status 'Completed (external stage)' in planned_burn_reports.

capture_body.description: Review D5: when set, this burn is an ARRIVAL/CAPTURE burn at the named body, and its ACTUAL fired ΔV is re-solved fresh at trigger time from the vehicle's real (dispersed) state — a VELOCITY-matching solve (scale the body-relative speed to local circular speed along the current relative-velocity direction; provably always yields a bound orbit), the genuinely different math a capture burn needs versus target_epoch_s's position-shaping Lambert re-solve. Requires a matching cruise_seed.body_tracks entry with a resolvable mu_m3s2 (explicit or catalog); mutually exclusive with target_epoch_s — both checked by check_config. Falls back to firing dv_inertial_mps verbatim if the runtime track lookup fails. Solved at trigger time only (not continuously re-solved through the slew — a velocity-matching target drifts far more slowly than a shrinking-TOF Lambert one).

label.description: Free-text label for telemetry/debugging only (e.g. "DSM leg 2", "Mercury capture") — never consulted by the executive itself.

PointingTargetConfig.description: Which inertial direction a PointingRuleConfig targets. Discriminated by `type`.

name.description: Only when type=Body — must have a matching BodyTrackConfig entry in cruise_seed.body_tracks.

direction.description: Only when type=Inertial — a fixed inertial direction.

PointingRuleConfig.description: One pointing rule: a placed hardware item's boresight/normal should point at target.

hardware_index.description: Index into spacecraft.hardware. Must resolve to a hardware type with a real pointing direction (StarTracker/OpNavCamera/Lidar/CommAntenna/SolarPanel/CustomPlate, with boresight/normal set if optional) — check_config rejects otherwise.

GncModeConfig.description: A named, prioritized pointing-rule set (a GNC "mode"). rules' LIST ORDER is the priority order — index 0 is highest/primary, index 1 is secondary (best-effort), index 2+ are evaluated only (cannot control the attitude — see docs/MP/MANUAL.md §6.4).

pointing_locked.description: Marks this mode's pointing as non-negotiable (Phase 13m item #4): when active, the TCM executive prefers RCS (no slew) over the main engine for a correction rather than reorienting off this mode's rules. Defaults to false (pre-existing behavior).

mode.description: Must match a name in cruise_seed.modes.

BodyTrackConfig.description: A precomputed heliocentric position track for one named body -- used for PointingTargetConfig::Body pointing resolution AND (added) real third-body gravitational perturbation in the cruise loop (see mu_m3s2), and optionally (also added) real SOI-switching central-body capture (see soi_capture).

track.description: Precomputed samples — OR omitted/empty (review B2 the SERVER-RESOLVED form): an empty track on a named ANISE-covered body asks the server to sample its own ephemeris over the leg duration before the job starts (4 samples/day, clamped to [64, 2000] points, consumed through cubic Hermite interpolation). The backend owns the kernels; shipping ephemeris client→server at client-chosen density is no longer necessary for any ANISE-covered body. A body without ANISE coverage still needs an explicit track. Since the Hermite upgrade, v_mps IS consulted (spline tangents) — supply real velocities.

epoch_jd.description: Review B2: epoch of t_s = 0 [Julian Date] for the server-resolved form — only consulted when track is empty. Defaults to trajectory.departure_epoch when null; an empty track with neither is a 422 (nothing anchors the sampling).

mu_m3s2.description: Gravitational parameter [m^3/s^2] -- lets this same track ALSO drive real third-body perturbation (see CruiseStepMsg.accel_third_body_mps2), not just pointing. null falls back to a body_models::TargetBody catalog lookup by name; if that also fails (a synthetic/non-physical track, e.g. a test fixture), this track is used for pointing only, silently excluded from the perturber list.

soi_capture.description: : registers this track as a real SOI-switching CENTRAL-BODY candidate in the cruise loop's propagated truth, not just a third-body perturber. false (default) preserves every prior behavior: soi_radius_m is always null for every body_track, so the propagator's own central-body resolution (crates/sim_engine::propagator6dof, reusing trajectory_solver::resolve_central_body) can never select it -- the cruise loop's truth state stays under Sun-only central gravity even through a real close approach. This was the confirmed root cause of a genuine captured orbit (e.g. around Mercury) reading as a flyby in a mission-validation replay: the reference trajectory (built from a real Phase-01 result) correctly showed the captured orbit, but the propagated TRUTH never switched central body, so dispersion against that reference blew up as if the spacecraft flew straight through. true sizes a real Laplace SOI radius (heliocentric distance at the track's first sample when the body's catalog primary is null, e.g. Mercury; distance from the primary's OWN body_track when primary is set and that track is also supplied, e.g. the Moon needs distance from Earth -- falls back to heliocentric distance with a server-side warning if the primary's track isn't present) and a real radius_m for the collision/close-approach check. check_config rejects soi_capture: true on a track whose body resolves no mu_m3s2 (neither an explicit override nor a body_models catalog match) -- setting the flag with no way to size an SOI would otherwise silently stay third-body-only, defeating the point without saying why.

CruiseStepMsg.description: One streamed cruise-loop tick, sent over /stream when the job's cruise_seed was set. A sibling of SimStepMsg, not a reuse — no navigation-filter fields (Phase 13h/navigation isn't built yet; this streams TRUTH state only), dispersion-against-reference and GNC-telemetry fields in their place (the design notes backlog item #6). msg_type (added, dispatch-hardening ask): distinguishes this from CruiseMcRunMsg at parse time -- a real client bug sent cruise_seed + monte_carlo_runs: 1, which server-side dispatches to the CruiseMc job kind instead, and the client blindly parsed the resulting CruiseMcRunMsg frames as this type and crashed reading r_m off an object without it. Which shape a job's stream carries was always decided by the request you made (cruise_seed alone vs. cruise_seed + monte_carlo_runs > 0); msg_type lets a consumer verify that assumption at parse time instead of trusting it got the request right.

msg_type.description: Always "cruise_tick" -- the discriminant that distinguishes this frame from CruiseMcRunMsg.

q.description: Attitude quaternion [w, x, y, z] — same layout convention as SimStepMsg.q.

q_cmd.description: The commanded/target attitude quaternion [w, x, y, z] this tick — what pointing_mode (or the active GncCommander rule solve) decided the spacecraft should be pointed at. q is what it actually achieved; the quaternion-PD control law drives the two together.

pointing_error_deg.description: Angle between current and commanded attitude (SunPointing, or the active GncCommander mode's solved attitude when cruise_seed.modes is non-empty).

torque_cmd_body_nm.description: Body-frame torque [N*m] the quaternion-PD law computed from (q, q_cmd, omega) BEFORE wheel-speed-saturation zeroing — what the controller wanted to apply.

torque_delivered_body_nm.description: Body-frame torque [N*m] actually applied this tick, post-saturation — what the controller could deliver given any wheel already pinned at its speed limit. Differs from torque_cmd_body_nm exactly when a wheel is saturated.

dr_m.description: |actual_r - reference_r| [m] at this tick — always reported; also actively corrected via TCM burns when cruise_seed.tcm_dr_threshold_m is set (item 5).

wheel_sat_frac.description: 0-1, fraction of max wheel speed (most-saturated wheel) — same formula as SimStepMsg.wheel_sat_frac.

wheel_torque_cmd_nm.description: Review E3 ( wire name pinned by the frontend's Fig. 5): the UNCLAMPED per-wheel motor-torque command [N·m] this tick's attitude demand implied (same wheel ordering as wheel_speeds_radps). Pair with wheel_torque_delivered_nm: when any wheel clamps, the delivered body torque differs from the commanded one in DIRECTION, which the speed-only wheel_sat_frac never shows. WheelsPrimary: the pure attitude command; ThrustersPrimary: the proportional unload command; ThrustersOnly: zeros.

wheel_torque_delivered_nm.description: Review E3: the DELIVERED per-wheel motor torque [N·m] — post ±max_torque clamp and speed-limit zeroing.

omega_radps.description: Body angular velocity [rad/s], body frame (ask bundled with E3) — same shape as the slew-test messages' omega_radps; the standard missing piece for diagnosing slew behavior.

planned_burn_idx.description: Which cruise_seed.planned_burns entry the current Slewing/Burning phase belongs to (burn-executive ask). null while coasting, RCS-correcting, or in a REACTIVE (dispersion-triggered) maneuver — so a reactive burn firing near a planned epoch is distinguishable from the planned burn itself.

planned_burn_fault.description: Set on exactly the tick a planned burn is declared missed ("MissedBurnTimeout": attitude not settled within the go/no-go window after its epoch — burn skipped, executive back to Coast). null otherwise.

wheel_torque_sat_frac.description: Review E3: max_i |wheel_motor_torque_cmd_nm[i]| / max_torque — the torque-authority twin of the speed-based wheel_sat_frac. Deliberately uncapped: EXCEEDS 1.0 when the demand overloads the wheels (the overload ratio is the useful signal).

propellant_remaining_kg.description: spacecraft.propellant_mass_kg minus rcs_propellant_kg_cum minus tcm_propellant_kg_cum — RCS desaturation pulses and (since) TCM burns are the two propellant sinks modeled; a translational burn beyond TCM correction is still not modeled.

torque_gravity_gradient_nm.description: Disturbance torque magnitude [N*m] from gravity-gradient, at this tick's environment (propagator6dof::disturbance_torque_breakdown, Phase 13b).

torque_srp_nm.description: Disturbance torque magnitude [N*m] from SRP (flat-plate only; 0 for a Cannonball-SRP vehicle, since cannonball SRP produces no torque by construction).

accel_central_gravity_mps2.description: Translational acceleration magnitude [m/s^2] from central-body gravity (point-mass + optional zonal), at this tick's environment (propagator6dof::translational_accel_breakdown).

accel_third_body_mps2.description: Real when cruise_seed.body_tracks resolves any perturber (a catalog-matched body name, or one with an explicit mu_m3s2) -- was structurally always 0.0 before since the cruise loop registered no third-body perturbers at all until then.

accel_srp_mps2.description: Always 0.0 in this first cut — SRP is not wired into translation for the decoupled step_tick path this loop uses (a documented, real Layer 1/Layer 2 fidelity gap, not an omission specific to this field).

active_mode.description: Phase 03 — which named GncModeConfig was active this tick. null when no GncCommander was supplied (legacy fixed-pointing-mode run) or the commander had no mode to select (no schedule/safe_mode coverage).

max_rule_violation_deg.description: Worst (largest) angular error among the active mode's rules beyond the top 2 (which cannot control the attitude — see docs/MP/MANUAL.md §6.4). null when no commander is active or the active mode has 2 or fewer rules.

tcm_phase.description: TCM executive state this tick (item 5): null while coasting/TCM disabled, "Slewing" while reorienting to burn attitude (takes priority over active_mode/pointing_mode), "Burning" while the finite burn is actually firing, "RcsCorrecting" while an RCS-only correction fires with no slew (item #4 pointing stays under normal control).

tcm_propellant_kg_cum.description: Cumulative main-engine propellant consumed by TCM burns [kg] — separate from rcs_propellant_kg_cum (a different propellant system, spacecraft.propulsion vs. RCS thrusters). Always 0.0 when TCM wasn't configured/never triggered.

tcm_dv_mps_cum.description: Cumulative REAL delivered TCM/burn translational ΔV [m/s] (frontend ask 2d) — Tsiolkovsky on the mass each burning tick actually lost, plus the projected RCS impulse per RcsCorrecting tick. Accumulated after the tick's row is built, so a tick's value covers everything through the PREVIOUS tick (same convention as the burning-tick half of tcm_propellant_kg_cum).

tcm_solve.description: The reactive-executive correction SOLVE that ran this tick, if any (frontend ask 2d) — a tick carrying one is always relayed regardless of report_stride, so DECLINED solves (which leave the phase in Coast and would otherwise be dropped by a coarse cruise stride) are visible on the stream too. null on the vast majority of ticks.

control_mode.description: Three-layer attitude control (MANUAL.md §10.5): the allocation mode actually used this tick (ThrustersPrimary during a main-engine burn).

controller_law.description: Layer-1 law that produced torque_cmd_body_nm this tick.

controller_kp.description: Effective k_p in force this tick (after activity tuning + scheduling); null for PhasePlane.

gain_schedule_point.description: Layer 3: set on exactly the ticks the active law was (re)derived; such ticks are always relayed regardless of report_stride.

ModeTransitionReport.description: One mode transition detected in a completed cruise run (Phase 03 'mode transitions are real slews with reported time/propellant/wheel cost'). settling_time_s uses the same threshold-crossing convention as /api/design/slew-test.

from_mode.description: null for the very first mode entered (transition from 'no mode').

settling_time_s.description: Time since the transition until pointing error first dropped to/below the settle threshold (0.5 deg) — null if it never did before the next transition or the run's end.

CruiseResult.description: Final result for a cruise-seeded /api/simulate job — a sibling of SimResult (no phase list, this loop flies one continuous leg; final/peak dispersion and wheel-momentum fields in its place).

max_dr_m.description: Peak position dispersion over the whole run.

tcm_propellant_kg_used.description: Cumulative main-engine propellant consumed by TCM burns [kg] (item 5) — 0.0 when TCM wasn't configured/never triggered.

cruise_csv_path.description: Local filesystem path, not an HTTP-fetchable URL — file serving isn't implemented yet.

mode_transitions.description: Empty when no GncCommander was active (legacy fixed-pointing-mode run).

reference_interpolation_floor_m.description: Review C2: empirical interpolation floor of the submitted reference [m] — leave-one-out cross-validation of the same cubic Hermite interpolation the cruise loop uses (reconstruct each interior sample from its two neighbors, max position error, divided by 16 for the O(Δt⁴) scaling from the 2Δt leave-one-out span to the production Δt span). An order-of-magnitude warning threshold, not a precise bound. null when the reference has fewer than 3 samples.

warnings.description: Review C2: human-readable configuration warnings that are not hard check_config errors. Currently: tcm_dr_threshold_m set below reference_interpolation_floor_m (TCM would partly chase interpolation noise rather than real dispersion — raise the threshold or supply a denser reference). Empty when nothing is worth flagging.

planned_burn_reports.description: One entry per cruise_seed.planned_burns item, in config order (burn-executive ask: real slew-start/ignition/completion epochs vs. the configured epoch, and missed-burn faults as reported findings). Empty when no planned burns were configured.

reactive_burn_reports.description: Frontend ask 2d: one entry per REACTIVE (dispersion-triggered) maneuver, in time order — trigger/ignition/completion epochs, the governing solve's targeting/iterations/convergence/final miss, executed ΔV and propellant — plus zero-ΔV entries for DECLINED trigger solves, so the executive's 'looked, chose not to fire' decisions are on the record. The reactive twin of planned_burn_reports; render next to those rows. Empty when reactive TCM never triggered.

attitude_control_effective.description: Three-layer attitude control (MANUAL.md §10.5): every derived/overridden law parameter the run actually used — a run is reproducible from this block.

gain_schedule_points.description: Layer 3: one entry per tick the active law was (re)derived, in time order. The same points are streamed on their ticks (CruiseStepMsg.gain_schedule_point), which are always relayed regardless of report_stride.

PlannedBurnReport.description: Execution report for one planned burn. The executive now starts the slew BEFORE the configured epoch by a computed lead time (kinematic slew time at the profiled cruise rate + a settle margin), HOLDS the inertially-fixed burn attitude, and ignites at the epoch (never before; late only if the attitude had not settled by then, in which case the ΔV is re-solved at actual ignition). If the attitude has not settled within a go/no-go window after the epoch, the burn is declared missed and skipped. All epochs are on the cruise_seed clock (the same t_s the tick stream uses) — compare directly against configured_epoch_s to diagnose early/late ignition without guessing which clock the executive triggered on.

slew_start_s.description: First Slewing tick for this burn — before configured_epoch_s when the lead-time scheduling caught it in time.

ignition_s.description: First Burning tick (real ignition). For a non-capture burn, >= configured_epoch_s by construction. For a capture_body burn, ignition is gated on the DISPERSED trajectory's own periapsis passage (hyperbolic Kepler, recomputed per tick), so it may precede or follow the stored epoch — firing a velocity-matching burn at the nominal clock time instead captured into whatever orbit the ship's current radius implied (measured: ignition at 13,998 km vs a 6,681 km planned periapsis bought a barely-bound a=261,617 km orbit).

completed_s.description: First Coast tick after the burn delivered its full ΔV. null for a missed burn.

status.description: NotReached: the leg ended before the burn's lead window opened. BurnAttitudeAbort: the burn was cut off after pointing >20° off for 30 s of burn time.

achieved_capture.description: Capture burns only (achieved-vs-planned ask): the orbit the burn ACTUALLY bought about its capture_body, from the truth's state at completion — compare against the Phase 01 result's post_capture_orbit_* fields. Null for non-capture burns, faulted/unreached burns, or an unresolvable body track.

bound.description: Specific orbital energy about the capture body is negative (a real capture).

ignition_radius_m.description: Body-relative radius [m] at ignition — the single number that decides what orbit a velocity-matching burn can buy.

sma_m.description: Semi-major axis [m]; null when not bound.

TcmSolveInfo.description: One reactive-executive correction SOLVE, reported on the tick it ran (frontend ask 2d) — previously 'solver converged' vs 'returned the guess' was only distinguishable via TCM_DEBUG on the server console. Carried on CruiseStepMsg.tcm_solve; the per-tick Slewing re-target solves are deliberately NOT reported (one per tick — noise, and never what actually fires): the trigger-time and ignition-time solves are.

context.description: Trigger: the Coast-phase dispersion trigger's solve. Ignition: the settled-attitude re-solve that decides what actually burns (the governing one for a main-engine correction). RcsTrigger: the RCS path's refine, which has no ignition step.

targeting.description: BPlane/Position: which shooting formulation refined the correction under the real force model (B-plane targeting at the approach body when the horizon is a reference SOI entry; fixed-time-of-arrival position targeting otherwise). Lambert: only the two-body guess was solved (the direct trigger path — refinement happens at ignition there).

aim_epoch_s.description: Epoch [s, cruise clock] the solve aimed at — the SOI entry for a B-plane solve, the bounded Lambert horizon otherwise.

lambert_dv_mps.description: |ΔV| [m/s] of the two-body Lambert guess the solve started from.

solved_dv_mps.description: |ΔV| [m/s] of the solve's own result — what the decision below was made on.

iterations.description: Newton iterations the shooting refinement actually performed — 0 with a shooting targeting means it returned the guess untouched. null when no refinement ran (targeting == Lambert).

converged.description: Whether the shooting refinement met its miss tolerance. null when no refinement ran.

miss_m.description: Final residual miss [m] at the aim point under the real force model.

no_burn_miss_m.description: Predicted delivery miss [m] with NO burn (B-plane path only) — the (2b) trigger metric; the approach trigger declines to correct when this is already within tcm_dr_threshold_m.

decision.description: What the executive did with the solve. ReSlew: the refined direction moved past the re-slew gate, so the vehicle re-slews instead of firing along the stale attitude. DeclinedDeliveryFine: no-burn miss already within threshold. DeclinedNotWorth: non-converged and not clearly halving the dispersion — a finding, not a maneuver.

ReactiveBurnReport.description: Per-reactive-maneuver execution report (frontend ask 2d) — the reactive twin of PlannedBurnReport, on CruiseResult.reactive_burn_reports. All epochs on the cruise_seed clock. The solve fields come from the maneuver's GOVERNING solve (the last ignition-time / RCS-trigger solve), except lambert_dv_mps which is always the trigger-time two-body guess.

trigger_epoch_s.description: First tick of the maneuver (Slewing/RcsCorrecting entry), or the declined solve's own tick.

actuator.description: None: a declined solve — nothing fired.

targeting.description: The governing solve's targeting — see TcmSolveInfo.targeting.

lambert_dv_mps.description: |ΔV| [m/s] of the trigger-time two-body Lambert guess.

predicted_miss_m.description: The governing solve's final residual miss [m] at its aim point.

ignition_s.description: First Burning/RcsCorrecting tick — null when nothing fired.

completed_s.description: First tick back in Coast — null when the leg ended mid-maneuver.

executed_dv_mps.description: Real delivered translational ΔV [m/s] over the maneuver — Tsiolkovsky per burning tick / projected RCS impulse per correcting tick, NOT the commanded impulse.

propellant_kg.description: Propellant this maneuver consumed [kg] (main-engine + RCS-TCM pool).

status.description: AbortedAtIgnition: the slew ran but the ignition re-solve refused to fire (non-converged / not worth it). Unfinished: the leg ended mid-maneuver (executed_dv/propellant then undercount the final tick).

CruiseMcRunMsg.description: One completed Monte Carlo run's result, sent over /stream when the job was started with cruise_seed set AND simulation.monte_carlo_runs > 0 (the design notes backlog item #10) -- one message per completed run, never per-tick, mirroring McRunMsg's convention. Disperses spacecraft.mass_kg, its inertia diagonal, (Cannonball SRP only) reflectivity, AND (added) real HardwareItem PLACEMENT geometry -- RcsThruster position/thrust-vector alignment and CustomPlate/placed-SolarPanel position/normal alignment (5mm/0.5deg and 1cm/1deg 1-sigma respectively) -- see cruise.rs's disperse_hardware_placement doc comment for the exact scope (sensor/antenna boresight dispersion is still NOT included). Placement dispersion isn't reported as its own field here (unlike mass_kg_used/reflectivity_used/inertia_diag_kgm2_used) since a vehicle can have an arbitrary number of dispersed hardware items -- its effect shows up through the same tracked outputs (max_dr_m, final_pointing_error_deg, max_wheel_momentum_nms, propellant_remaining_kg).
