IMPORTANT: in the current physics model (no burns, SRP not wired into translation), mass/reflectivity dispersion has NO effect on any tracked output (gravity is mass-independent; Cannonball SRP produces zero torque by definition) -- inertia and RCS/plate-geometry dispersion are the axes with a real, currently-observable effect (RCS placement/alignment on propellant efficiency and control authority; plate geometry on SRP torque under FlatPlate only). msg_type (added) distinguishes this from CruiseStepMsg at parse time -- see that schema's own description for the real bug this prevents.

msg_type.description: Always "cruise_mc_run" -- the discriminant that distinguishes this frame from CruiseStepMsg.

reflectivity_used.description: null when the vehicle's SRP model isn't Cannonball.

CruiseMcSummaryResult.description: Final summary once all cruise Monte Carlo runs complete -- analogous to McSummaryResult for the body-centric MC path.

mc_summary_csv_path.description: Local filesystem path, not an HTTP-fetchable URL.

ArcApiPoint.description: One sampled point along a propagated transfer arc, for 3D visualization. Units: metres, SI.

central_body.description: Which body was gravitationally central at this point (Phase 7k SOI-switching). "Sun" when the spacecraft was outside every candidate body's SOI (the reference frame), else the name of the body whose SOI it was inside.

leg_idx.description: For MGA results: 0-indexed leg number this point belongs to (leg 0 = departure body to first flyby, leg 1 = first flyby to second, etc.). null for single-leg GA/PSO results.

vx_mps.description: Real velocity x-component [m/s], same frame as x_m/y_m/z_m. Always present as of: GA/PSO transfer arcs, every pre_departure_orbit_arc/post_capture_orbit_arc (both search methods), AND MGA's own multi-leg arc (its sampling now keeps the velocity it always computed). Still typed nullable for results saved before the respective field landed.

launch_vehicle_check.description: Added. Only present for the "cruise_heliocentric" entry (the departure leg) on an Earth departure with a real configured vehicle — always null for "body_centric_loi" (an arrival/capture burn, not a departure).

arc.description: Sampled transfer-ellipse path (60 points). NOTE: orientation is synthetic — departure is placed along an arbitrary +x axis since Hohmann's analytical model has no real inertial-frame context. Shape/timing are physically correct; absolute direction is not tied to real heliocentric/body-fixed axes. Contrast with BestArcApiResult.arc, which uses real ephemeris-derived positions.

dv_arr_ms.description: Objective-aware arrival ΔV [m/s] (frontend backlog #14/#15): 0.0 for a Flyby mission — Flyby never burns to arrive, mirroring OptimizeApiResult.dv_arrival_ms's convention on the Phase 9 real-dynamics path. For Orbit/Landing, a real vis-viva capture burn (√(v∞²+2μ/r_p) − √(μ(1+e)/r_p), r_p floor-clamped to the target body's physical radius — the same formula mga_scan_run.rs::capture_dv_ms and mga.rs::arrival_dv_ms use) when [trajectory.capture].target_orbit_radius_m is configured, else the raw arrival v∞ as a fallback. Rendezvous/SampleReturn are unchanged: the raw arrival v∞ (Rendezvous's arrival burn is deliberately a full relative-velocity match, not a periapsis-radius capture).

dv_total_ms.description: dv_dep_ms + dv_arr_ms, using the objective-aware dv_arr_ms above.

v_inf_arr_ms.description: Raw hyperbolic excess speed at arrival [m/s] — a physical quantity, never objective-adjusted (unlike dv_arr_ms).

dv_budget_ms.description: Onboard propellant pool only (Tsiolkovsky) — never includes launcher-provided ΔV. See launch_vehicle_check for the separate launcher pool.

budget_margin_ms.description: dv_budget_ms minus the onboard ΔV this trajectory actually requires — the PRICED arrival burn (dv_arr_ms, not the raw v∞: a sign error fixed) plus whatever part of the parking-orbit escape burn the launcher does not cover. Same number as dv_ledger.budget_margin_ms; kept for backward compatibility.

dv_ledger.description: Two-pool ΔV ledger (Phase 14e). Null only when the departure body is not in the body catalog.

launch_vehicle_check.description: Added. Non-null only for an Earth departure with a real, catalog-recognized [spacecraft].launch_vehicle configured.

arc.description: Sampled transfer-arc path (60 points), real heliocentric departure/arrival positions — not synthetic, unlike HohmannApiResult.arc. Empty if the Lambert re-solve at the best point unexpectedly failed.

dv_total_ms.description: dv_dep_ms + dv_arr_ms, using the objective-aware dv_arr_ms below.

dv_arr_ms.description: Objective-aware arrival ΔV [m/s] (frontend backlog #14/#15) — same convention as BestArcApiResult.dv_arr_ms: 0.0 for Flyby, a real vis-viva capture burn for Orbit/Landing (falling back to the raw arrival v∞ if [trajectory.capture].target_orbit_radius_m isn't configured), raw arrival v∞ unchanged for Rendezvous/SampleReturn.

v_inf_arr_ms.description: Raw hyperbolic excess speed at arrival [m/s] — a physical quantity, never objective-adjusted (unlike dv_arr_ms).

MonteCarloSampleApiResult.description: One Monte Carlo sample. Only the stride-selected subset (~30 of the full scatter) carries a `trajectory`; the rest have `trajectory: null` and scalar fields only.

trajectory.description: Sparse propagated trajectory (~18-19 points), only for the stride-selected subset. Monte Carlo never gets the dense per-sample stream — see the design notes.

MonteCarloApiResult.description: Local Gaussian-scatter robustness probe around the porkchop best point (Phase 2 scope, not a full state/hardware Monte Carlo). Populated only when `solver = "MonteCarlo"`.

reference_dv_total_ms.description: Porkchop-best ΔV total this scatter is centered on.

OptimizerApiResult.description: Best individual/particle from a GA or PSO search over (departure offset, TOF). Populated only when `solver = "GA"` or `"PSO"`.

fitness.description: Value minimized: C3 [km²/s²] for Flyby, ΔV total [m/s] otherwise.

dv_budget_ms.description: Onboard propellant pool only (Tsiolkovsky) — never includes launcher-provided ΔV. See launch_vehicle_check for the separate launcher pool.

budget_margin_ms.description: Same number as dv_ledger.budget_margin_ms (kept for backward compatibility).

dv_ledger.description: Two-pool ΔV ledger (Phase 14e). Null only when the departure body is not in the body catalog.

launch_vehicle_check.description: Added. Non-null only for an Earth departure with a real, catalog-recognized [spacecraft].launch_vehicle configured.

sun_hat_body.description: Spacecraft->Sun unit direction, ALREADY IN THE BODY FRAME (this endpoint does not resolve attitude/heliocentric geometry itself). Set to also receive the srp section of the response; omit (or null) to get mass properties only.

sun_distance_m.description: Heliocentric distance [m], only affects the radiation-pressure magnitude used for srp (not direction). Defaults to 1 AU when omitted.

label.description: e.g. "Bus/structure (+ propellant, unmodeled subsystems)" or "SolarPanel #0" — the bus/structure remainder is always contributions[0].

position_m.description: Relative to the geometric-center origin, NOT the CoM.

inertia_about_com_kgm2.description: This component's own contribution to the total inertia tensor, about the TRUE CoM. Full symmetric 3x3, row-major [[Ixx,Ixy,Ixz],[Ixy,Iyy,Iyz],[Ixz,Iyz,Izz]] — generally non-diagonal for any off-axis component (point-mass parallel-axis form).

center_body_m.description: Plate centre relative to the geometric-center origin, as built by simulate.rs::build_plates (see VehicleProperties' own frame-consistency note: this is NOT re-expressed relative to the derived CoM).

force_n.description: Real per-plate SRP force vector [N], body frame, from orbital_models::flat_plate_force_per_plate — the actual flat-plate law (blends incidence direction and plate normal per rho_s/rho_d), not a magnitude-only or incidence-direction approximation. Exactly [0,0,0] for a plate facing away from the Sun (not omitted from the list).

p_srp_nm2.description: Radiation pressure [N/m^2] used, from sun_distance_m (or 1 AU default).

cop_m.description: Center of pressure: the force-magnitude-weighted centroid of illuminated plates, for THIS sun direction — moves as the sun direction changes, unlike a static geometric centroid. (CoP - CoM) is the real SRP disturbance-torque arm. Relative to the geometric-center origin, same frame as com_m. null only if literally no plate is illuminated (e.g. a degenerate/zero-area config).

mass_kg.description: Total spacecraft mass — always equals the request config's spacecraft.mass_kg exactly.

com_m.description: Center of mass, relative to the geometric-center origin (the bus centroid, [0,0,0] by definition).

inertia_kgm2.description: Full inertia tensor about the TRUE CoM, row-major, generally non-diagonal (sum of every ComponentContribution's own inertia_about_com_kgm2). Real off-diagonal terms are expected and physically meaningful once any component sits off a principal axis — do NOT assume this reduces to the old hand-typed spacecraft.inertia_diag_kgm2's 3 numbers. UPDATE: the running 6DOF simulation CAN now use this tensor's diagonal — set spacecraft.derive_inertia_from_geometry = true on the request config (see SpacecraftConfig) to make the live sim's inertia match this endpoint's own computation exactly. Off-diagonal (cross-coupling) terms are still not consumed anywhere — SpacecraftProperties remains diagonal-only by signature. Without that flag set, the sim still uses spacecraft.inertia_diag_kgm2 unchanged, and this value stays purely informational for that request.

contributions.description: contributions[0] is always the bus/structure remainder (spacecraft.mass_kg minus every itemized hardware mass, clamped at 0); one entry per [[spacecraft.hardware]] item after that, in config order.

warnings.description: Non-fatal issues, e.g. itemized hardware mass exceeding spacecraft.mass_kg (the bus/structure remainder was clamped to 0 rather than going negative).

srp.description: Present only when the request set sun_hat_body.

main_engine_torque_check.description: Review E5, backend half: static main-engine-vs-RCS feasibility. null when the config has no spacecraft.propulsion.

MainEngineTorqueCheck.description: Static (no dynamics) feasibility of holding attitude through a main-engine burn: the engine (body +X, mounted at the -X bus face — cruise.rs's fixed convention) produces a disturbance torque r_offset × F_thrust about the CoM (the SAME arm the live simulation flies with, cruise::main_engine_thrust_offset_body_m); RCS must cancel it during ThrustersPrimary. rcs_authority_nm is the placed layout's achievable torque along the cancellation axis (same thruster selection the live allocator uses, full duty, projected onto that axis). If ratio exceeds 1, every burn tumbles the vehicle by physics, not by bug — warn in the Phase 02 builder and before a Phase 03 run.

thrust_offset_body_m.description: Engine mount point minus CoM, body frame [m].

rcs_authority_nm.description: Achievable RCS torque along the cancellation axis [N·m]. When the disturbance is zero, the layout's weakest-axis authority over ±x/±y/±z probes instead (a general capability number). 0 with no RCS configured.

ratio.description: disturbance_torque_nm / rcs_authority_nm — > 1.0 means this engine/RCS combination cannot hold attitude during a burn. null when a real disturbance exists but the layout has zero authority along the needed axis (worse than any finite ratio).

feasible.description: true when there is no disturbance to cancel, or ratio <= 1.0.

SlewTestInitialStateRequest.description: Round-2 slew-test. See SlewTestRequest.initial_state's own description for the semantic switch this triggers.

initial_error_deg.description: In [0, 180]. Default 90. Role depends on initial_state: with initial_state OMITTED, this offsets the STARTING attitude away from the fixed commanded target (q0 = dq * q_cmd). With initial_state PRESENT, this instead offsets the COMMANDED TARGET away from the fixed nominal (q_cmd = dq * nominal) -- see initial_state's own description for why.

axis.description: Rotation axis (inertial frame, re-normalized server-side) paired with initial_error_deg -- see that field's description for which quantity it offsets. Default [0,0,1].

control_mode.description: Default WheelsPrimary. ThrustersOnly (round-2) fully excludes the wheel cluster from control -- zero motor torque, zero reaction, zero momentum-dump activity -- the true RCS-only isolation test (neither WheelsPrimary nor ThrustersPrimary actually isolates RCS: WheelsPrimary lets wheels do the work, ThrustersPrimary still actively drives wheels toward zero speed every tick, a real nonzero reaction torque). See sim_engine::ControlMode.

kp.description: Quaternion-PD proportional gain. Defaults to the config's own [gnc] reaction_wheel_kp (pd_gains_from_cfg) when omitted.

kd.description: Quaternion-PD derivative gain. Defaults to the config's own [gnc] reaction_wheel_kd when omitted.

tick_s.description: Control tick [s]. Default 5.0, clamped server-side to [0.1, 60].

duration_s.description: Simulated duration [s]. Default 1800, clamped server-side to [tick_s, 7200].

settle_threshold_deg.description: Pointing error below which the response's settling_time_s is recorded. Default 0.5.

initial_state.description: Round-2. Seeds this call's STARTING attitude/rate directly from a previous call's real ending state (its last sample's q/omega_radps) instead of the canned q0 derivation -- this is what makes a chained sequence of slew-test calls a genuinely continuous 'chase a moving target' animation rather than a jump-cut back to a fresh nominal start every call. When present, initial_error_deg/axis are reinterpreted to offset the COMMANDED TARGET instead of the starting attitude (a fixed target the vehicle already reached would otherwise make every subsequent call start at ~0 error). wheel_speeds_radps and mass_kg are NOT seeded from any prior call -- always the config's own defaults (zero speeds, full spacecraft mass). When set, its own omega_radps takes priority over initial_omega_radps outright (not summed).

initial_omega_radps.description: Round-2. Body-frame angular rate [rad/s] to start a FRESH (non-chained) run with, one independent value per axis. Default [0,0,0] (the original behavior). A step response from rest can't surface a control gap on an axis whose initial ERROR happens to start near zero (e.g. a rank-deficient thruster layout that's structurally uncontrollable about one axis); a real, persistent initial SPIN on a specific axis is what actually probes control authority there. Only applied when initial_state is NOT set -- when initial_state IS set, its own real omega_radps (genuine continuity data) takes priority outright, not summed with this field.

rcs_duty_cycle.description: 0-1, this tick's aggregate RCS pulse-width duty cycle (0 unless the tick fired RCS, e.g. ThrustersPrimary/ThrustersOnly mode or a wheel-desaturation pulse).

q.description: Real attitude quaternion [w, x, y, z] at this sample -- same convention as every other quaternion field in this API (e.g. SimStepMsg.q, CruiseStepMsg.q). Added for a non-approximated attitude-replay animation of the slew test.

omega_radps.description: Real body-frame angular velocity [rad/s] at this sample.

thruster_duty_cycles.description: Round-2: per-thruster PWM duty cycle [0,1] this tick, indexed IDENTICALLY to the placed-thruster list rcs_from_hardware builds from the request config (zip against that same ordering to know which physical thruster this index is). Every SELECTED (torque-aligned) thruster shares the same nonzero value as rcs_duty_cycle; unselected thrusters are 0.0. Empty array iff the config has no RCS hardware at all.

controller_law.description: Three-layer attitude control: the slew test now flies the SAME per-mode registry the cruise loop does (MANUAL.md §10.5), so a ThrustersPrimary/ThrustersOnly test exercises the RCS-authority-derived thruster law. Explicit kp/kd in the request force a plain Pd override.

kp.description: Effective proportional gain flown; null for PhasePlane.

settling_time_s.description: Simulated time [s] at which pointing error first dropped to/below settle_threshold_deg. null if it never settled within duration_s.

overshoot_deg.description: How far above settle_threshold_deg the error climbed again after first settling (0 if it stayed under). null iff settling_time_s is null.

max_wheel_momentum_nms.description: Peak wheel-cluster momentum magnitude over the run -- compare against the configured wheel cluster's saturation threshold to check for desaturation events.

wall_clock_ms.description: Real wall-clock time [ms] the server spent computing this result -- useful for budgeting a future Monte Carlo sweep over many slew tests.

q_command.description: Round-2: the fixed target attitude [w, x, y, z] every sample's error_deg is measured against for this run -- constant for the whole call (a fixed step test), hence top-level rather than per-sample. See SlewTestSample.q for the actual/live attitude to compare it against.

samples.description: Decimated time series (capped at 300 points) for plotting.

job_id.description: Monotonic counter, not a UUID — process-lifetime unique only

step.description: Steps streamed so far. null once done.

total_steps.description: Always null in v1 — no upfront estimate is computed. Treat as indeterminate progress, not a percentage.

cancelled.description: true once POST.../cancel has been called for this job (Phase 9k task 4). For a single-run simulate job this reliably means the run stopped early — the truth-integration loop polls the cancellation flag every truth step. For a Monte Carlo job (monte_carlo_runs > 0) this only reflects that cancellation was *requested*: the already-dispatched batch of runs (spawned via thread::scope, joined together) is NOT interrupted mid-flight, a known architectural limitation — see MissionPlanner/src/server/routes/simulate.rs's module doc comment.

SimStepMsg.description: One streamed step, throttled to measurement cadence (dt_meas_s). Sent as a JSON text frame over the /stream WebSocket.

q.description: Attitude quaternion [w, x, y, z], body -> inertial/Hill frame

wheel_sat_frac.description: 0-1, fraction of max wheel speed (most-saturated wheel)

lidar_residual_m.description: null if LIDAR isn't configured or didn't return a measurement this step

nav_csv_path.description: Local filesystem path, not an HTTP-fetchable URL — file serving isn't implemented yet

attitude_csv_path.description: Local filesystem path, not an HTTP-fetchable URL

maneuvers_csv_path.description: Local filesystem path, not an HTTP-fetchable URL

McTrajPoint.description: One body-centric point along a Monte Carlo run's sparse trajectory (~18 points, time-stride-sampled) — deliberately not the dense per-step SimStepMsg feed.

McRunMsg.description: One streamed message per completed Monte Carlo run, sent as a JSON text frame over /stream when the job was started with monte_carlo_runs > 0 — never a per-truth-step message.

trajectory.description: Present only for a stride-selected subset of runs (capped at 20 regardless of monte_carlo_runs); null for all other runs.

McSummaryResult.description: Final result for a Monte Carlo job (monte_carlo_runs > 0), analogous to SimResult for a single-run job.

mc_summary_csv_path.description: Local filesystem path, not an HTTP-fetchable URL

OptimizationBody.description: One SOI-candidate or third-body-perturber entry for the optimization stage's force model — the user-specified equivalent of what /api/design/trajectory infers automatically from target_body/third_bodies.

role.description: CentralWhenInSoi: this body becomes the propagator's central body whenever the spacecraft is inside its Laplace sphere of influence (real SOI-switching). AlwaysThirdBody: always a point-mass perturber, never a central-body candidate.

fidelity.description: Central-body gravity fidelity, only meaningful when role = CentralWhenInSoi. Must be null/omitted for AlwaysThirdBody (third-body perturbers are point-mass only by design). Numeric j2/j3/j4 values always come from the body_models catalog, not user-supplied — falls back to PointMass with a server-side warning if the catalog lacks matching harmonic/pole data for the body.

srp.description: Default false. Not yet wired into the Phase 9 fitness evaluator — reserved for a future fidelity upgrade.

integrator.description: Only Dopri5 is actually implemented by the underlying propagator today; other values are accepted by the schema but not yet honored.

bodies.description: Additional third-body perturbers / SOI candidates beyond the departure and target bodies, which are *always* auto-registered as CentralWhenInSoi candidates regardless of this list. May be omitted or empty — no longer required to be non-empty.

GaParams.description: Required when optimization.method = "GA". No defaults — every field must be supplied.

mutation_rate.description: Peak per-gene mutation probability — decays via cosine schedule to 10% of this value by the final generation.

PsoParams.description: Required when optimization.method = "PSO". No defaults — every field must be supplied.

ShootingParams.description: Required when optimization.method = "MultipleShooting". Schema-only today — the method itself is not implemented yet and the job will fail at run time with a clear error.

SequenceSearchConfig.description: Tisserand beam-search configuration for automatic intermediate-body discovery (Phase 9j). When present under optimization.mga.sequence_search, the optimizer discovers flyby body sequences automatically from candidate_bodies rather than requiring the user to specify flyby_bodies explicitly. The outer Tisserand beam search prunes the discrete sequence space; the inner DE optimizer runs on each top-ranked candidate sequence. mga.flyby_bodies is ignored when sequence_search is set.

candidate_bodies.description: Pool of body names to consider as intermediate flyby targets. Each must be a catalog body with a known semi-major axis. Repeated visits (e.g. Venus→Earth→Earth→Jupiter) are allowed — list each body once.

max_legs.description: Maximum number of legs (= max intermediate flybys + 1). Keep ≤ 6 for reasonable run time.

beam_width.description: How many partial sequences to keep alive at each depth level of the Tisserand tree. Larger = more thorough outer search. Default: 25.

max_sequences_to_optimize.description: How many top-ranked Tisserand sequences to run the full inner DE optimizer on. Default: 8.

vinf_departure_estimate_ms.description: Approximate departure v∞ [m/s] used to seed the Tisserand graph walk. A rough estimate is fine; the inner optimizer finds the true value. Default: 5000.

MgaParams.description: Required when optimization.method = "MGA". Implements MGA-1DSM (one deep-space manoeuvre per leg) with Differential Evolution/SHADE/MBH as the inner optimizer (Phase 9d-9g, 9x-v). The full leg sequence is [optimization.departure_body] + flyby_bodies + [optimization.target_body]. Set sequence_search to have the optimizer discover flyby bodies automatically via Tisserand beam search (Phase 9j) instead of specifying them manually.

flyby_bodies.description: Intermediate bodies only, in visit order — excludes the overall departure_body/target_body. Ignored when sequence_search is set. Optional — defaults to [] when omitted (Phase 9k-v bug #2 fix: previously omitting this field entirely caused a 400 with an opaque JSON parse error, even though it was already documented as optional here).

leg_tof_days.description: One [min, max] TOF range [days] per leg. When sequence_search finds fewer legs than entries here, the last entry is used as a fallback.

departure_vinf_max_ms.description: Maximum allowed departure v∞ from the departure body [m/s]. Default: 15000.

departure_vinf_min_ms.description: Minimum allowed departure v∞ from the departure body [m/s] (Phase 9v-iii). Default 0.0 = unconstrained. Must satisfy 0 <= min < departure_vinf_max_ms. Prevents degenerate near-zero departure burns (the GTOP Cassini-2 benchmark bounds departure v∞ to [3, 5] km/s).

flyby_min_periapsis_m.description: Minimum periapsis radius [m] for any intermediate gravity-assist flyby. Must be > flyby body surface radius. Default: 6371000 (Earth radius).

arrival_vinf_max_ms.description: Maximum acceptable arrival v∞ at the final body [m/s]. Candidates exceeding this are penalised in the real-objective phase. Default: 25000.

rp_norm_bounds.description: Per-leg [min, max] periapsis bound override (units of that flyby body's radius), one entry per intermediate flyby (flyby_bodies.length entries, one fewer than leg_tof_days). Default null, which keeps the historical uniform (1.05, 300.0) bound for every flyby regardless of body. Added to let a specific benchmark config (e.g. the real GTOP Cassini-2 problem, whose official bounds per Izzo & Vinkó 2008 Table IV differ sharply per body: Venus [1.05, 6], Earth [1.15, 6.5], Jupiter [1.7, 291]) reproduce the exact official search box instead of the generic, much wider default.

eta_max.description: Upper bound override for every leg's DSM-timing fraction η. Default null, which keeps the historical 0.99 upper bound. The real GTOP Cassini-2 problem uses 0.9 (Table IV) — set this to 0.9 to match exactly when reproducing that benchmark. Added alongside rp_norm_bounds for the same reason.

de_f_weight.description: DE mutation scale factor F ∈ [0.4, 1.0]. Default: 0.8.

de_generations.description: Total DE generation budget (shared across phase 1 restarts and phase 2). Default: 1000.

de_restarts.description: Number of independent phase-1 restarts. Default: 3.

de_seed.description: Base RNG seed for the DE search (Phase 9v-vii). Restart r uses de_seed + r*137; phase 2 uses de_seed + de_restarts*137. Default 42 reproduces the historical hardcoded seeding. Vary across runs to measure seed-to-seed spread.

de_adaptive.description: Use SHADE self-adaptive DE (success-history F/CR adaptation + current-to-pbest/1 with archive; Tanabe & Fukunaga 2013) instead of classic fixed-parameter DE/rand/1/bin. When true, de_f_weight/de_cr seed the success-history memory rather than being fixed. Default: true.

sequence_search.description: When set, auto-discovers flyby body sequences via Tisserand beam search instead of using flyby_bodies.

min_solar_perihelion_m.description: Minimum heliocentric perihelion [m] permitted for either sub-arc of any leg (the departure Kepler sub-arc or the Lambert sub-arc) — rejects chromosomes whose orbit dives unrealistically close to the Sun. Distinct from flyby_min_periapsis_m (closest approach to a flyby body, not the Sun). Default: 0.2 AU (2.991957414e10 m).

scan.description: Phase 9w ballistic (no-DSM) powered-flyby grid scan config — the middle tier between Tisserand sequence pruning and the DE-based MGA-1DSM search. Optional: when present, the mga-scan CLI subcommand (and POST /api/mga-scan) can run a deterministic launch-window scan for this mission's flyby sequence before (or instead of) running the DE/MBH search.

pruning.description: Phase 9x incremental pruning (Ceriotti 2010, Ch. 3) — an optional leg-by-leg pre-search that seeds Phase 1's DE restarts instead of (or alongside) the existing seeded/random restarts. Optional: when absent, run_mga behaves exactly as before (no pruning).

search_method.description: Phase 9x-v Stage 3: which global search algorithm runs Phase 2 (the real-objective refinement). Mbh (Monotonic Basin Hopping, default as of Stage 4) beat matched-budget DE by 40-57% on both head-to-head validation missions (VEEGA 1989, Cassini-2 GTOP) — see docs/MP/BENCHMARKS.md "Search method comparison". De remains available as an explicit opt-in for A/B comparison. Default: Mbh.

mbh.description: MBH configuration, used only when search_method = "Mbh". Optional — omitting takes the documented defaults.

SearchMethod.description: Which global search algorithm runs MGA-1DSM Phase 2 (Phase 9x-v Stage 3). See trajectory_solver::mbh for the algorithm itself. Default: Mbh.

MbhConfig.description: Configuration for the Phase 9x-v Monotonic Basin Hopping search method. See trajectory_solver::MbhSolver for the algorithm itself. All fields optional — every field has a documented default, so an empty object is valid.

hops.description: Number of hops per chain (after each chain's initial local descent). Default: 200.

perturb_fraction.description: Fraction of chromosome variables perturbed on each kick. Default: 0.3.

kick_scale.description: Kick magnitude as a fraction of each variable's bounds width. Default: 0.15.

local_max_iter.description: Max local-descent iterations per hop (both the initial descent and every post-kick refinement), for whichever local_optimizer is selected. Default: 500.

seed.description: RNG seed for the kick sequence. Default: 42.

stop_after.description: Early-stop-on-stagnation: a chain terminates after this many consecutive non-improving hops instead of always burning its full hops budget. null (default) disables early stop. Added per the real pagmo2 MBH default (stop = 5, src/algorithms/mbh.cpp).

local_optimizer.description: Which local optimizer runs MBH's inner descent step. NelderMead (default, unchanged prior behaviour), CompassSearch (a best-of-all-directions pattern search, added), or HookeJeeves (a greedy accept-first-improving pattern search with an evaluation-budget termination, added — real MBH reference implementations default to a very shallow per-hop descent of this kind, not a full local solve).

hooke_jeeves.description: HookeJeevesSearch configuration, used only when local_optimizer = "HookeJeeves". Defaults reproduce a real, independently-verified MBH reference implementation's own default inner-descent behaviour exactly (a fresh reimplementation, not a port — see the Third-Party Algorithm Reimplementation Policy).

extra_random_chains.description: Extra purely-randomly-initialised chains added alongside the elite seeds (pruning survivors + bidirectional-backfit stitches). 0 (default) is byte-identical to prior behaviour. Added: when non-zero, the outer search is no longer 100% dependent on the pre-search having found the right basin.

global_stall.description: Global-relative early stop: abandon a chain once past global_stall.patience hops if it's still worse than the best result any chain has found so far by more than global_stall.margin_frac. null (default) disables this — byte-identical to prior behaviour. Added after finding that stop_after alone lets a chain keep dodging its own consecutive-failure counter indefinitely while being globally irrelevant.

migration.description: Archipelago-style migration: every migration.interval of a chain's own hops, a chain whose incumbent is worse than the live global best by more than migration.margin_frac receives the global best as its new incumbent and keeps hopping from there with its own kick stream. Where global_stall kills a losing chain, migration repurposes it. Promoted to a standard default (enabled = true) after a same-seed A/B on Cassini-2 showed it strictly helped two of three resonance-family branches and never hurt the winning branch — see the design notes Phase 9x-v. Set enabled = false to restore previous behaviour exactly.

MbhLocalOptimizer.description: Which local optimizer runs MbhSolver's inner descent step. See MbhConfig.local_optimizer. Default: NelderMead.

HookeJeevesConfig.description: Configuration for trajectory_solver::HookeJeevesSearch. See MbhConfig.hooke_jeeves. All fields optional with real reference-implementation defaults.

max_fevals.description: Fitness-evaluation budget per local descent (NOT an iteration count). 1 (default) is a real, independently-verified reference-implementation default, not a placeholder — it produces a near-single-probe descent, deliberately leaving nearly all exploration work to the outer MBH hop loop.

start_range.description: Initial step size, as a fraction of each parameter's bounds width. Default: 0.1.

stop_range.description: Stop once the (normalised) step size drops below this. Default: 0.01.

reduction_coeff.description: Step shrink factor applied after a full sweep finds no improving move. Default: 0.5.

GlobalStallConfig.description: Configuration for trajectory_solver::MbhSolver's global-relative early stop. See MbhConfig.global_stall. Both fields required when this object is provided (no defaults).

patience.description: Hops a chain is allowed past which it is abandoned if still worse than the live global best by more than margin_frac.

margin_frac.description: Fractional margin (relative to the live global best) beyond which a past-patience chain is considered globally irrelevant and abandoned.

MigrationConfig.description: Configuration for trajectory_solver::MigrationConfig. See MbhConfig.migration. All fields optional.

enabled.description: true (default) = migration active with the parameters below. Set false to disable — reproduces previous behaviour.

interval.description: How often (in a chain's own hops) a migration check runs. Default: 10.

margin_frac.description: Fractional margin (relative to the live global best) beyond which a chain is migrated onto the global best. Default: 0.3.

PruningConfig.description: Configuration for the Phase 9x incremental pruning pre-search. See crates/trajectory_solver/src/incremental_pruning.rs for the generic engine and the design notes Phase 9x section for the motivation. All fields optional.

samples_level0.description: Number of random samples drawn at level 0 (departure + leg-0 vars). Default: 2000.

children_per_survivor.description: Number of random continuations sampled per surviving parent at every level after 0. Default: 50.

max_survivors_per_level.description: Hard cap on survivors carried into the next level (bounds total evaluation count — keeps the search polynomial in level count). Default: 40.

threshold_factor.description: Pruning threshold as a multiple of the best partial cost found at that level. "Generous" is intentional (Ceriotti's own term) — this discards clearly-bad prefixes, not just the single best one. Default: 3.0.

n_seeds.description: Number of best survivors (by partial cost) fed as elite seeds into the existing Phase 1 DE restarts. Default: 8.

bidirectional.description: Bidirectional ("meet in the middle") extension (Phase 9x): alongside forward leg-by-leg pruning, run a mirror-image backward pass from the target and inject the best stitched full chromosomes as additional Phase 2 seeds — generic promotion of the backward-fit decomposition that hand-solved Galileo's VEEGA. Default: true; set false for A/B isolation runs.

bound.description: Admissible remaining-cost bound (branch-and-bound extension): before the forward pruning pass, run a small backward suffix sampling per intermediate split and bin the cheapest suffix cost found; the forward pass then prunes on cost_so_far + bound (A*'s f = g + h) instead of cost-so-far alone (the GASP mechanism, Myatt et al. 2004; Izzo et al. 2007). null (default) = today's purely greedy behaviour, byte-identical. Deliberately NOT promoted to a default (unlike surrogate/migration) — its own A/B was mixed and a bound+surrogate stack regressed further as budget grew — see the design notes Phase 9x-v.

surrogate.description: Surrogate-assisted child sampling: reuse the evaluations pruning already performs by fitting a per-level RBF model to (child vars → added cost) pairs and drawing several candidate children per slot, keeping only the best-predicted one for real evaluation (Jones et al. 1998 EGO paradigm; Regis & Shoemaker 2007 RBF variant). Promoted to a standard default (enabled = true) after beating plain sampling on every tested branch — see the design notes Phase 9x-v. Set enabled = false to restore previous (plain-sampling) behaviour exactly.

PruningBoundConfig.description: Configuration for the pruning remaining-cost bound. See PruningConfig.bound. All fields optional.

safety_frac.description: Fraction of the sampled suffix-cost bound that is discounted before use, hedging the gap between a sampled minimum (an overestimate of the true minimum) and an admissible bound: h = bin_min * (1 - safety_frac). 0.0 trusts the sampled minimum outright; larger is safer but prunes less. Default: 0.5.

epoch_bins.description: Bins over the interface-epoch axis of each split's bound table. Default: 24.

vinf_bins.description: Bins over the interface-|v∞| axis of each split's bound table. Default: 12.

samples_per_split.description: Backward samples drawn per split to build the table (full-length suffixes, cheapest-per-bin retained). Default: 3000.

PruningSurrogateConfig.description: Configuration for surrogate-assisted pruning sampling. See PruningConfig.surrogate. All fields optional.

enabled.description: true (default) = surrogate-assisted sampling active. Set false to disable — reproduces previous (plain-sampling) behaviour.

oversample_factor.description: Candidate children drawn per child slot; only the best-predicted one is really evaluated. Default: 4.

min_fit_samples.description: Minimum recorded (vars, cost) pairs at a level before the surrogate is trusted; below this, sampling is plain (first candidate kept). Default: 60.

length_scale.description: Gaussian-kernel length scale in normalized [0,1] units. Default: 0.3.

MgaScanConfig.description: Configuration for the Phase 9w ballistic (no-DSM) powered-flyby MGA grid scan. Scans a departure-date x per-leg-TOF grid with pure Lambert legs and analytic powered-flyby feasibility (no DSMs, no propagation, no optimizer) — see the design notes Phase 9w and trajectory_solver::mga_scan for the model.

horizon_years.description: Scan horizon centered on optimization.departure_epoch, spanning ± horizon_years/2 years.

tof_grid_points_per_leg.description: Number of TOF grid points per leg, spanning that leg's optimization.mga.leg_tof_days bounds. Default: 40.

flyby_dv_max_ms.description: Prune branches whose per-flyby powered-flyby matching burn exceeds this [m/s] — the scan's "v∞-match tolerance" expressed as a ΔV cost. Default: 3000.

max_records.description: Safety cap on stored feasible branches. Default: 500000.

job_id.description: Monotonic counter, not a UUID — process-lifetime unique only. Separate counter from /api/simulate's and /api/optimize's job IDs.

MgaScanRecordApi.description: One feasible complete branch found by the scan — mirrors one row of mga_window_scan.csv.

dep_mjd2000.description: Departure epoch, days since the MJD2000 epoch (JD 2451544.5).

vinf_arr_ms.description: Arrival hyperbolic excess speed at the final target body [m/s].

sum_flyby_dv_ms.description: Sum of flyby_dvs_ms — the branch's total powered-flyby matching-burn cost [m/s].

capture_dv_ms.description: Vis-viva capture burn from vinf_arr_ms into [trajectory.capture]'s configured orbit around the target body — null when that section/field isn't set (e.g. a Flyby mission has no orbit to capture into). Total cost is vinf_dep_ms + sum_flyby_dv_ms for a Flyby-style trajectory (no arrival burn), or + capture_dv_ms for an Orbit-style trajectory (with a real capture burn) — the caller picks which, since both are legitimate depending on mission type.

leg_tofs_days.description: One entry per leg, leg order (departure_body -> flyby_bodies... -> target_body).

flyby_dvs_ms.description: Powered-flyby matching burn at each intermediate body [m/s] — one entry per flyby body (length = body_sequence.length - 2).

flyby_rp_km.description: Solved shared periapsis radius at each flyby [km].

flyby_turn_deg.description: Total turn angle achieved at each flyby [deg].

n_records_dropped.description: Feasible branches beyond optimization.mga.scan.max_records, discarded rather than returned.

RankedSequenceApi.description: One candidate flyby sequence found by the Tisserand beam search.

flyby_bodies.description: Intermediate flyby bodies only, in visit order (excludes the departure and target bodies, which are the chain's overall endpoints). Empty for the direct (zero-flyby) case.

estimated_vinf_arr_ms.description: Estimated v∞ at the target body from the Tisserand graph walk [m/s] — a rough estimate; the inner DE/scan finds the true value.

tisserand_score.description: Cumulative Tisserand feasibility score (lower = better). This is the list's sort key — `sequences` is always sorted ascending by this field.

sequences.description: Every candidate sequence the beam search found, sorted by tisserand_score ascending (best first) — not just the top pick.

OptimizationConfig.description: Phase 9 trajectory optimization stage (Layer 1b) — real propagated-dynamics optimization, distinct from trajectory's closed-form narrowing-stage solvers (Hohmann/Lambert/GridSearch/MonteCarlo/GA/PSO). Carries its own independent copy of departure epoch/window fields, NOT derived from `trajectory`'s. The departure burn is NOT anchored to a Lambert-solved v-infinity (that would make the GA/PSO search trivially converge to the analytic Hohmann-like minimum — not a meaningful test of global search). Instead it's four independent, freely-searchable numbers: departure_offset_days (which day — sets the departure/target synodic alignment), and three burn parameters at a circular parking orbit: burn location (true anomaly, full range, no config knob), burn magnitude (dv_min_ms..dv_max_ms), and an out-of-plane angle (full range — handles the real plane change to the target's orbit). Reaching the target at all is therefore a genuine search outcome, not a foregone conclusion.

objective.description: Distinct from mission.objective (Flyby/Orbit/Landing/etc, the MISSION objective) — this is the scalar the Phase 9 optimizer minimizes under real propagated dynamics. MinC3/MaxMassMargin (originally 4th/5th options) were dropped: for a fixed spacecraft, both are deterministic monotonic functions of the same total ΔV MinDeltaV already uses, carrying zero independent optimization signal. MatchTargetDistance minimizes the difference between the real closest-approach distance to the target body and trajectory.capture.target_orbit_radius_m (required when this objective is selected) — the right objective for Flyby/Orbit, where the goal is a specific flyby/capture distance, not hitting the target exactly.

method.description: Distinct from trajectory.solver's GA/PSO (closed-form Lambert-proxy search) — these variants evaluate real propagated dynamics inside the fitness loop, a materially different cost profile despite the shared algorithm name. GA and PSO use real-propagated single-leg dynamics; MGA uses the MGA-1DSM model (Phase 9d-9j, fully implemented) with a selectable Phase-2 global search algorithm (mga.search_method: DE/SHADE or MBH — Monotonic Basin Hopping, the default since Phase 9x-v Stage 4). MultipleShooting is recognized but not implemented yet and will fail at job run time with a clear error.

departure_body.description: Catalog body name (must be ANISE-covered — see /api/bodies). Also the start of the MGA leg chain when method = "MGA".

target_body.description: Catalog body name (must be ANISE-covered). Also the end of the MGA leg chain when method = "MGA" — intermediate flyby bodies are configured separately under mga.flyby_bodies.

departure_epoch.description: ISO 8601, e.g. "2026-09-15T00:00:00 UTC". Required for the job to actually run (enforced at run time, not at /api/validate).

departure_window_days.description: Search window width [days] centered on departure_epoch. Omit/null for a fixed departure epoch (window = 0).

dv_min_ms.description: Minimum departure burn magnitude to search [m/s].

dv_max_ms.description: Maximum departure burn magnitude to search [m/s].

theta_min_deg.description: Burn-location angle theta search range minimum [deg] — user-configurable search-variable ranges. Defaults to 0 (with theta_max_deg defaulting to 360: the full circle, the previous hardcoded behavior). check_config requires 0 <= min < max <= 360.

theta_max_deg.description: Burn-location angle theta search range maximum [deg] — see theta_min_deg.

phi_min_deg.description: Out-of-plane angle phi search range minimum [deg] — defaults to -45 (with phi_max_deg defaulting to +45, the previous hardcoded range). check_config requires -90 <= min < max <= 90.

phi_max_deg.description: Out-of-plane angle phi search range maximum [deg] — see phi_min_deg.

max_coast_days.description: How long to coast and watch for a close approach to the target body before giving up [days] — a ceiling, not a prescribed transfer duration. The achieved time-to-target is an output of the search (see OptimizeApiResult.achieved_tof_days), not an input.

mga.description: Required when method = "MGA". Configures the MGA-1DSM optimizer (DE inner solver, two-phase search, optional Tisserand sequence discovery).

job_id.description: Monotonic counter, not a UUID — process-lifetime unique only. Separate counter from /api/simulate's job IDs.

step.description: Generations (GA) or iterations (PSO) completed so far. null once done.

total_steps.description: Known upfront from optimization.ga.generations or optimization.pso.iterations — unlike /api/simulate's status, this is usually a real number, not always null. null for MGA (whose step count is determined dynamically by de_restarts × de_generations) and for MultipleShooting.

cancelled.description: true once POST.../cancel has been called for this job (Phase 9k task 4). Honored by GA/PSO (checked every generation/iteration, plus every pass of the post-search coordinate-descent refinement) — the job stops within roughly one generation and /result returns whichever candidate was best so far, not an error. NOT honored by MGA (method = "MGA") — its DE search has no cancellation hook yet; cancelled still flips true, but the in-flight compute runs to completion regardless. See MissionPlanner/src/optimize.rs's optimize_api_with_progress doc comment.

OptimizeStepMsg.description: One streamed step — sent as a JSON text frame over the /stream WebSocket. Deliberately no propagated arc (see the design notes Monte Carlo streaming rule, applied here too) — the arc is computed once, in /result.

step.description: 0-indexed generation (GA) or iteration (PSO). Since (GA): ONE unified generation counter that never exceeds the configured [optimization.ga].generations budget — the internal restart structure's gen-0 callbacks re-emit the current index instead of inflating it, and the post-search coordinate-descent refinement no longer streams steps at all (its polish still lands in /result). A client can safely set its x-axis to the configured budget.

phase.description: 1 (GA's internal closest-approach bootstrap phase), 2 (real-objective refinement; PSO always 2), or 3 (the post-search coordinate-descent refinement pass, all emitted at step = the configured budget -- render distinctly, e.g. red). Since informational/diagnostic only: best_fitness is on ONE unit across phases.

best_fitness.description: Best-so-far value of the configured objective in its NATURAL units (since second revision same day — no Hohmann normalization on the wire): MinDeltaV → total ΔV [m/s]; MinTof → achieved TOF [days]; MatchTargetDistance → |closest − target| [km]. Selection internally still uses the normalized fitness; this is the displayable value of the same best candidate. f64::MAX serialization (~1.8e308) is the 'nothing feasible yet' sentinel, same as before. For MGA jobs, unchanged: total ΔV [m/s].

best_params.description: The best decision-variable vector found so far. MGA (method = "MGA"): the raw MGA chromosome (see mga.rs's chromosome layout doc comment), Phase 9k task 1. GA/PSO (since previously always null for these methods): the 4-vector [dep_offset_days, theta_burn_rad, dv_departure_ms, phi_out_of_plane_rad] matching bounds_from's parameter order — the live search-variable convergence plot's data source. null only on early steps before any feasible candidate exists. CORRECTION (Phase 9k "step-stream context"): under a FIXED flyby_bodies sequence (sequence_search not set) the sequence is constant for the whole job and a client only needs departure offset + per-leg TOF/eta to decode a schematic path. Under sequence_search auto-discovery, the sequence is NOT constant — several candidate sequences are optimized in turn within one job — so a client MUST track the most recent MgaSequenceContextMsg to know which real flyby_bodies these params decode against.

mga_legs.description: Per-leg trajectory state (DSM position/velocity, arrival velocity, arrival v-infinity) for best_params, one entry per leg in leg order — MGA (method = "MGA") only, backlog item #18. Every quantity here is already computed as an ordinary byproduct of chromosome fitness evaluation (mga_leg.rs's MgaLegResult); it is re-extracted once per streamed generation (not once per fitness evaluation) so a live-replay client can draw the REAL solved Lambert arc / DSM point / flyby geometry for the best-so-far chromosome, instead of client-side reconstructing an approximate, Lambert-branch-blind re-solve from best_params alone. null for GA/PSO (no leg concept). For an MGA job this can still be an empty array on a generation whose best chromosome happened not to be evaluable — treat that the same as "no leg detail this generation", not as a different job type.

population.description: This generation's full evaluated population (each entry one parameter vector, same [dep_offset_days, theta_burn_rad, dv_departure_ms, phi_out_of_plane_rad] layout as best_params) — GA jobs only: the live search-space scatter plots' data source, so the full generation clouds render DURING the run, not only after completion via population_log. FEASIBLE individuals only, parallel to population_outcomes. null for PSO (its solver exposes only the global best per iteration) and MGA.

population_outcomes.description: Per-individual outcome pairs [dv_arrival_ms, tof_days], parallel to (same length/order as) population — GA jobs only: the outcome scatter plots' data source (departure vs arrival ΔV, departure offset vs coast time). Recorded as fitness-evaluation side-products, zero extra propagation cost. null whenever population is null.

best_feasible_value.description: Best objective value among FEASIBLE-capture candidates seen so far, scanned across every individual of every population (natural units, same as best_fitness) —: null until the first candidate whose approach periapsis lies inside the target's SOI exists. The convergence plot's solid line; best_fitness is the dashed may-be-infeasible lower bound (a borderline-outside-SOI candidate can hold the fitness lead while feasible solutions exist elsewhere in the population). For MGA: mirrors best_fitness.

MgaLegStepInfo.description: Per-leg trajectory state for one evaluated MGA chromosome, extracted from mga_leg.rs's MgaLegResult (backlog item #18). Streamed inside OptimizeStepMsg.mga_legs for MGA jobs only.

r_dsm_m.description: Spacecraft position at the deep-space maneuver point [m], heliocentric [x, y, z].

v_dsm_after_mps.description: Spacecraft velocity just after the DSM [m/s], heliocentric — the Lambert-arc departure velocity that seeds segment B of this leg.

v_arrival_helio_mps.description: Spacecraft heliocentric velocity at leg arrival (Lambert arc endpoint, before subtracting the next body's velocity).

v_inf_arr_mps.description: Hyperbolic excess velocity on arrival relative to the next body [m/s] — feeds the flyby turn at an intermediate body, or the arrival v-infinity at the final target. Useful for a live flyby-turn indicator.

MgaSequenceContextMsg.description: A separate announcement frame, NOT a step — interleaved into the same /stream WebSocket as OptimizeStepMsg (Phase 9k "step-stream context" ask). Fires once per candidate flyby-body sequence for an MGA job, sent BEFORE the OptimizeStepMsg frames for that sequence's own generations arrive. Never sent for GA/PSO jobs. Distinguish from OptimizeStepMsg on the wire by the presence of msg_type — OptimizeStepMsg never carries that field, so no existing consumer parsing OptimizeStepMsg directly is affected by this addition.

msg_type.description: Always "mga_sequence" — the discriminant that distinguishes this frame from OptimizeStepMsg.

seq_idx.description: 0-indexed position of this sequence among the candidates being optimized this run.

seq_count.description: Total candidate sequences being optimized this run (>= 1; also 1 for the non-sequence_search fixed-sequence path).

flyby_bodies.description: The real flyby-body sequence about to be optimized (excludes the overall departure_body/target_body — same convention as MgaParams.flyby_bodies / the interior of OptimizeApiResult.mga_body_sequence).

is_direct_baseline.description: True for the always-included zero-flyby direct baseline the Tisserand beam search compares every gravity-assist candidate against (Phase 9j-B). False for every other sequence, including the fixed-sequence (non-auto) path.

OptimizeApiResult.description: Best result from a Phase 9 real-dynamics optimization search. For GA/PSO: a single-leg trajectory with real departure, heliocentric coast, and optional arrival/capture leg. For MGA: a multi-leg gravity-assist trajectory with one DSM per leg, found via MGA-1DSM + DE/SHADE/MBH, then refined by multiple shooting (Phase 9k task 3) — arc/fitness/mga_dv_dsms_ms reflect the multiple-shooting-corrected trajectory, not the raw search result. MGA-specific fields (mga_body_sequence, mga_dv_dsms_ms, mga_dsm_positions_m, mga_leg_tofs_days, mga_phase1_history, mga_ms_converged) are populated for MGA and null for GA/PSO.

method.description: Short code, matches optimization.method. (MultipleShooting is recognized in config but not implemented — the job fails before producing a result.)

objective.description: Human-readable label of optimization.objective, e.g. "Minimize ΔV".

theta_burn_rad.description: True anomaly of the departure burn at the parking orbit [rad] — one of the four search parameters.

dv_departure_ms.description: Departure burn magnitude [m/s] — the search parameter itself, not derived from any Lambert solve.

phi_out_of_plane_rad.description: Out-of-plane angle of the departure burn [rad] — handles the real plane change to the target's orbit. In Launch departure mode (Phase 14b) this slot is the asymptote's DLA [rad] and theta_burn_rad its RLA [rad]; dv_departure_ms is then the tangential injection burn the launch geometry derives (the gene itself is the v∞).

departure_mode.description: [trajectory.departure].mode (Phase 14a/14d). ParkingOrbit: the spacecraft starts in a given orbit and the departure burn is its own (free burn genes). Launch: the mission starts from a launch site, the launcher's upper stage delivers the injection (departure = launcher pool), and the search's departure genes are the asymptote (v∞, RLA, DLA) with the parking orbit/injection derived by closed-form launch geometry.

departure_dv_pool.description: Who pays dv_departure_ms — dv_ledger.departure_dv_pool surfaced at top level so a Phase 03 consumer can set external_stage on the departure burn without digging into the ledger. Null only when dv_ledger is.

injection_epoch_jd.description: Epoch of the injection burn [JD] — equals dep_jd (the departure fires at the departure epoch; the parking-orbit coast in pre_departure_orbit_arc precedes it).

launch_geometry.description: Launch departure mode only (Phase 14c/14d): closed-form launch geometry for this result's own departure asymptote — RLA/DLA, the site-feasible plane, launch azimuth, coast angle and the exact injection state (MANUAL.md §13.6). Null in ParkingOrbit mode. A schematic ascent drawn from it is display only — pre_departure_orbit_arc stays the physical parking-orbit coast and is what Phase 03 references.

escape_duration_s.description: Real time spent escaping the departure body's SOI [s]. arc's first points with t_s <= escape_duration_s are the departure-body-centered escape leg; everything after is the heliocentric cruise leg — useful for a frontend camera stage that zooms in on departure, then out for cruise, then in again on arrival.

achieved_tof_days.description: Time of mission completion [days]: the capture burn's time if one was needed and achieved, else the time of closest approach to the target (the natural "arrival" moment for a Flyby). An output of the search, not a prescribed input — contrast the narrowing stage's tof_days, which is a chosen Lambert parameter.

dv_arrival_ms.description: Real arrival/capture burn [m/s] — a tangential insertion burn at trajectory.capture.target_orbit_radius_m, computed from whatever real incoming trajectory the search actually produced (not separately targeted). 0.0 for a Flyby mission (no capture burn exists to charge).

capture_time_s.description: Absolute time of the capture burn [s since departure], if one was needed and achieved. null for a Flyby.

capture_dv_inertial_mps.description: Real inertial ΔV VECTOR for the capture burn [m/s] -- a tangential (retrograde) insertion burn opposing the real incoming relative-velocity direction, magnitude exactly dv_arrival_ms. null for a Flyby, or for MGA (not computed there yet), or any candidate that didn't achieve a real capture.

departure_dv_inertial_mps.description: Real inertial ΔV VECTOR for the DEPARTURE burn [m/s] — the departure-side mirror of capture_dv_inertial_mps, so Phase 03 can prepend pre_departure_orbit_arc to the cruise reference and actually FIRE the departure at t_s = arc[0].t_s instead of treating the parking orbit as visual-only. As a velocity difference it needs no body-relative-to-inertial frame conversion. GA/PSO: post-burn minus pre-burn state from the exact circular_orbit_burn_state construction the search used — |v| equals dv_departure_ms by construction. MGA: the tangential periapsis escape burn, v0_hat * dv_escape from mga_departure_injection_state. null only when the departure body doesn't resolve (mirrors pre_departure_orbit_arc).

theta_arr_rad.description: Arrival-side mirror of theta_burn_rad — true anomaly of the capture burn. null for a Flyby or any candidate that didn't achieve a real capture.

phi_arr_rad.description: Arrival-side mirror of phi_out_of_plane_rad. null for a Flyby or any candidate that didn't achieve a real capture.

fitness.description: Dimensionless, normalized: ΔV/Hohmann-reference for MinDeltaV, achieved-TOF/Hohmann-reference for MinTof, |closest_approach - target_orbit_radius_m| / target_orbit_radius_m for MatchTargetDistance. No longer mixes raw units. For MGA (method = "MGA"): total ΔV [m/s] (departure + DSMs + arrival) AFTER the multiple-shooting refinement (Phase 9k task 3) — see mga_ms_converged.

miss_km.description: Real closest-approach distance to the target body over the whole arc (departure leg + cruise leg + arrival leg) [km] — not just the distance at some prescribed end point. The narrowing stage's GA/PSO (OptimizerApiResult) has no equivalent of this field — its Lambert-only arc always ends exactly on target by construction, so it cannot miss.

target_r_arr_m.description: Target body's real heliocentric position at the moment of closest approach (or capture) [m] — plot this alongside arc's last point to visualize the miss distance. For MGA (method = "MGA"): computed as the final body's real ANISE-queried heliocentric position at dep_jd + achieved_tof_days (Phase 9k-v bug #1 fix — this was hardcoded to [0,0,0] for every MGA result before, which put the target body on top of the Sun in the frontend's 3D view).

convergence.description: Best-fitness-so-far per generation (GA) or iteration (PSO) — phase 2's (real-objective) history for GA. Same units as phase 2 in OptimizeStepMsg, NOT the same scale as phase1_convergence_km.

phase1_convergence_km.description: Phase 1's (flyby-only) best-closest-approach-so-far history [km], one entry per generation across all restarts combined. Empty for PSO (no phase-1 split).

objective_history.description: The EXACT natural-units series the live convergence plot drew, persisted for reload/preset rendering — one [step, phase, value] row per sentinel-free streamed step: step on the unified budget-bounded generation counter, phase 1/2/3 (3 = the post-search refinement entries including the final polished value), value in the objective's natural units (MinDeltaV m/s, MinTof days, MatchTargetDistance km). The old `convergence` field is the internal normalized phase-2-only fitness history — a DIFFERENT series; prefer this one for display. Empty for MGA and for results saved before this field existed.

population_log.description: GA: every evaluated individual across both phases. PSO: empty. MGA (Phase 9k task 5): the best-so-far chromosome per generation — one row per phase1_history/convergence entry (MGA has no per-individual population exposed here, only DE/SHADE/MBH's running best) — generation is 0-indexed WITHIN each phase (unlike GA's population_log, whose generation matches the live-streamed OptimizeStepMsg.step value globally across restarts). The raw data for an x/y scatter of any two search parameters, colored by generation.

arc.description: Real propagated trajectory at the best point. For GA/PSO: departure leg + heliocentric cruise, under the configured force_model; leg_idx is null on all points. For MGA (Phase 9k task 3): the multiple-shooting-refined arc (real N-body perturbers via build_mga_perturber_entries, Newton/LM-corrected DSMs and flyby geometry — converged or best-effort, see mga_ms_converged) — heliocentric, all points labelled central_body="Sun", leg_idx carries the 0-indexed leg number. Falls back to the uncorrected Dopri5 repropagation (or the Keplerian/Lambert arc) only if the multiple-shooting refinement itself errors out (rare).

mga_body_sequence.description: MGA only: full body-name sequence, e.g. ["Earth","Venus","Jupiter"]. Length = number of legs + 1. null for GA/PSO.

mga_dv_dsms_ms.description: MGA only: per-leg DSM ΔV magnitudes [m/s], AFTER the multiple-shooting refinement (Phase 9k task 3) when it succeeded — falls back to the uncorrected search-time DSM magnitudes if the refinement errored out. Length = number of legs. null for GA/PSO.

mga_dv_dsms_inertial_mps.description: MGA only: real inertial ΔV VECTORS for each leg's DSM [m/s] — mga_dv_dsms_inertial_mps[k].norm == mga_dv_dsms_ms[k] by construction. Same source/fallback convention as mga_dv_dsms_ms (multiple-shooting-corrected when available, else freshly evaluated from the uncorrected search-time chromosome) — what a downstream consumer actually fires as a cruise_seed.planned_burns entry, instead of reconstructing a direction client-side. null for GA/PSO, or if the fallback evaluation itself fails.

mga_dsm_positions_m.description: MGA only: heliocentric [x, y, z] position [m] of each leg's DSM burn — the uncorrected search-time position (multiple shooting corrects the DSM's ΔV vector, not a separately-reported position). Length = number of legs. Use alongside mga_body_sequence to locate burn markers between body encounters. null for GA/PSO.

mga_dsm_epochs_s.description: MGA only: per-leg DSM epochs [s since departure, same clock as arc's t_s] — the missing epoch half of mga_dv_dsms_inertial_mps, so Phase 03 can populate cruise_seed.planned_burns without inferring epochs by matching mga_dsm_positions_m against arc. mga_dsm_epochs_s[k] = (leg k's start + eta_k * tof_k) in seconds; pairs index-for-index with mga_dv_dsms_inertial_mps / mga_dsm_positions_m. Valid for the multiple-shooting-refined arc too — MS's free variables are DSM ΔVs and node states, never the leg timing, and its transit-time offsets cancel algebraically at the DSM instant. null for GA/PSO.

mga_leg_tofs_days.description: MGA only: per-leg time-of-flight [days]. Length = number of legs. Sum equals achieved_tof_days. null for GA/PSO.

mga_phase1_history.description: MGA only: phase-1 (DSM-only fitness, m/s sum of all DSM ΔVs) best-fitness history across all DE restarts. Distinct scale from convergence (phase 2, total ΔV). null for GA/PSO.

mga_ms_converged.description: MGA only (Phase 9k task 3): whether the multiple-shooting refinement that produced arc/fitness/mga_dv_dsms_ms converged (Newton-Raphson within MAX_MS_ITER iterations) or is a best-effort, not-fully-corrected result — the refinement always returns SOME arc either way, this just says how much to trust it. null for GA/PSO. Also null for MGA if the refinement itself errored out entirely (rare — e.g. the winning chromosome's initial state was infeasible), in which case arc/mga_dv_dsms_ms fall back to the uncorrected search-time values instead.

mga_flyby_dv_gained_ms.description: MGA only (user-requested): the real ΔV [m/s] each intermediate flyby actually delivered, measured directly from the converged, real-dynamics-propagated trajectory -- |v_helio_at_SOI_exit - v_helio_at_SOI_entry| (not an analytic re-derivation from v-infinity-in/v-infinity-out; propagate's output is always in one consistent heliocentric frame regardless of which body was internally central during integration). Length = number of intermediate flyby bodies (mga_body_sequence minus departure/target). null under the same conditions as post_capture_orbit_arc: not MGA, or mga_ms_converged is not true -- no genuinely converged flyby passage to measure.

mga_flyby_speed_before_ms.description: Paired with mga_flyby_dv_gained_ms: real heliocentric speed [m/s] just before each flyby's real SOI entry. Compare against mga_flyby_speed_after_ms to see whether a given flyby added or removed heliocentric energy. Same length/gating as mga_flyby_dv_gained_ms.

mga_flyby_speed_after_ms.description: Paired with mga_flyby_speed_before_ms: real heliocentric speed [m/s] just after each flyby's real SOI exit. speed_after > speed_before means that flyby ADDED heliocentric energy (taken from the planet's own orbit, by conservation of momentum); speed_after < speed_before means it REMOVED energy (given back to the planet) -- the real, checkable signature of an energy-shedding deceleration flyby (e.g. MESSENGER's resonant Mercury passes). Same length/gating as mga_flyby_dv_gained_ms.

post_capture_orbit_arc.description: Phase 12c, upgraded same day by 9y-h: the actual resulting orbit around the target body AFTER the capture burn — re-seeded with a post-burn velocity at the crossing/arrival point and propagated for 2 full orbital periods. Fixed (Phase 12k): points are now in the SAME heliocentric frame `arc` uses (the target body's own real heliocentric position at the capture epoch has already been added to every point) — this field used to return raw target-body-relative meters with `arc`'s heliocentric frame documented as separate/not-to-be-concatenated, which forced any consumer wanting one continuous path to drop these points rather than mix frames (confirmed as the real cause of a captured orbit reading as a flyby in a downstream replay that tried to build its reference trajectory from this data). central_body is still always the target body's own name (e.g. "Mars") — that field means "which body's gravity is locally dominant here," not "which frame this position is in." GA/PSO: the orbital plane is derived from the real propagated crossing state (r_rel × v_rel of the actual inbound trajectory). MGA: since 9y-h gave multiple shooting's final leg a real, non-degenerate target to converge onto (previously it targeted the arrival body's exact center), the orbital plane now also comes from a REAL propagated crossing state (`mga.rs::ms_arrival_relative_state`, re-propagating only the converged final leg) — the same construction as GA/PSO, not a modeling convention. Falls back to the pre-9y-h ecliptic-proxy convention (coplanar with the target body's own instantaneous heliocentric orbit) only in the rare case that real-state re-propagation itself fails despite mga_ms_converged being true. null for: any mission objective other than "Orbit"/"Landing" (Flyby has no capture burn; Rendezvous/SampleReturn aren't modeled as a periapsis-radius capture); an Orbit/Landing candidate that never achieved a real capture crossing; and — MGA only — whenever mga_ms_converged is false or null (building a resulting orbit on top of a physically-uncorrected or gap-filled trajectory would compound a bad foundation with a fabricated-looking orbit, so it's omitted rather than computed from the uncorrected arc).

post_capture_orbit_period_s.description: Orbital period [s] of post_capture_orbit_arc, computed analytically from the same inputs used to build the ring (not derived from the sampled points) -- so a frontend can show "period: X hours" directly instead of re-deriving it from raw geometry. Same presence/null gating as post_capture_orbit_arc itself (user-requested).

post_capture_orbit_periapsis_m.description: Periapsis radius [m] of post_capture_orbit_arc. For MGA this is the real configured/priced target_orbit_radius_m (or its floor-clamped value); same for single-leg. Equal to post_capture_orbit_apoapsis_m whenever post_capture_orbit_eccentricity is 0 (circular, the common case).

post_capture_orbit_apoapsis_m.description: Apoapsis radius [m] of post_capture_orbit_arc -- periapsis_m * (1+e)/(1-e). Equal to post_capture_orbit_periapsis_m when circular.

post_capture_orbit_eccentricity.description: Eccentricity of post_capture_orbit_arc — derived from the REAL post-burn state: the real arrival velocity direction, speed scaled to the configured capture orbit's periapsis speed √(μ(1+e)/r) (Phase 14f: the single-leg GA/PSO/MBH path now honors [trajectory.capture].capture_eccentricity in BOTH the priced dv_arrival_ms/capture_dv_inertial_mps and this ring, as MGA and the survey already did). Equals the configured e for a tangential crossing; reports the real, slightly different shape when the crossing has a radial component.

post_capture_orbit_sma_m.description: Semi-major axis [m] of post_capture_orbit_arc (user-requested Kepler-element summary) — derived from the same real post-burn state the propagated ring itself was seeded with.

post_capture_orbit_inclination_deg.description: Inclination [deg] of post_capture_orbit_arc's plane to the reference frame's fundamental plane (the J2000 frame every state in this pipeline is expressed in), acos(h_z/|h|) of the real post-burn state.

pre_departure_orbit_arc.description: Phase 12 (user-requested): the real parking orbit leading up to the departure burn, propagated for 2 full orbital periods, so the frontend can show where the spacecraft actually started instead of the arc beginning abruptly mid-escape. Fixed (Phase 12k): points are now in the SAME heliocentric frame `arc` uses (the departure body's own real heliocentric position at the departure epoch has already been added to every point) — previously returned as raw departure-body-relative meters, documented as a separate frame not to be concatenated with `arc`. central_body is still always the departure body's own name — that field means "which body's gravity is locally dominant here," not "which frame this position is in." GA/PSO uses the REAL parking orbit the search found (r_park_m/theta_burn_rad/the real orbital plane), ending exactly at the real burn point. MGA (`mga.rs::mga_departure_injection_state`) decodes the winning chromosome's already-optimized departure v∞ vector and constructs the real periapsis-injection state via the same closed-form hyperbolic-departure math GA/PSO uses — a real parking orbit at the correct radius/plane, not a stand-in. This is display-only: the search itself still has no committed burn-location/timing degree of freedom for MGA departure (12j, still open — `departure_escape_dv_ms` only prices a scalar ΔV magnitude). Always present when the departure body resolves (does not depend on mission objective or mga_ms_converged — every optimized mission has a departure leg). Purely additive/display — does not change any reported ΔV number.

launch_vehicle_check.description: Launch-vehicle check at THIS result's own departure C3 (Phase 14d-lite — the frontend used the survey's best_arc.launch_vehicle_check as a stand-in before). GA/PSO: C3 from the search's own injection state (|v_post|² − 2μ/r_park); MGA: from the chromosome's departure v∞ via mga_departure_injection_state. Null for a non-Earth departure, no [spacecraft].launch_vehicle, an unknown vehicle name, or a departure body that doesn't resolve.

dv_ledger.description: Two-pool ΔV ledger + propellant feasibility (Phase 14e) for this result: departure = dv_departure_ms (split launcher/onboard per launch_vehicle_check), DSMs = sum of mga_dv_dsms_ms (MGA) or 0, arrival = dv_arrival_ms. Null only when the departure body doesn't resolve.

PopulationLogRow.description: One evaluated individual from a Phase 9 GA or MGA search (empty for PSO). Raw data behind an x/y-scatter-colored-by-generation plot.

phase.description: 1 (flyby-only search), 2 (real-objective refinement), or 3 (post-search coordinate-descent refinement probes -- all logged at generation = the configured budget) — same meaning as OptimizeStepMsg.phase.

generation.description: GA: absolute generation index (phase 1's independent restarts and phase 2 share one continuously-increasing index, no overlap), matching the live-streamed OptimizeStepMsg.step value. MGA (Phase 9k task 5): 0-indexed WITHIN each phase instead — NOT globally aligned with OptimizeStepMsg.step, a documented deviation from GA's convention.

params.description: GA: always 4 entries, [dep_offset_days, theta_burn_rad, dv_mps, phi_out_of_plane_rad]. MGA: the raw chromosome vector (see mga.rs's chromosome layout doc comment) — length varies with leg count (2 + 5*n_legs), NOT fixed at 4.

fitness.description: This individual's fitness (km for phase 1, dimensionless normalized for phase 2 on GA; for MGA, phase 1 is the DSM-only sum in m/s and phase 2 is total ΔV in m/s — see OptimizeApiResult.mga_phase1_history/convergence). f64::MAX (~1.7976931348623157e+308) marks an infeasible individual — filter these out before plotting, same sentinel convention as OptimizeApiResult.fitness.

dv_arrival_ms.description: This individual's own arrival burn [m/s] (real crossing burn, or the capture-into-any-orbit burn at its closest approach; 0.0 for a Flyby mission) — recorded as a fitness-evaluation side-product for the outcome scatter plots (departure vs. arrival ΔV). null for an infeasible candidate, MGA rows, and rows from before this field existed.

tof_days.description: This individual's own achieved time of flight [days] (capture time, or closest-approach time when it never captured) — same outcome recording (departure offset vs. coast time scatter). null for an infeasible candidate, MGA rows, and rows from before this field existed.
